articles.title: Raízen fecha acordo de R$ 22,4 bilhões com a União e abate R$ 8,5 bilhões em multas e juros | G1
articles.standfirst: Do total negociado, R$ 16,7 bilhões são de responsabilidade da empresa. Após o desconto em multas e juros, a Raízen usará créditos fiscais e pagará R$ 2,5 bilhões à vista para quitar sua parcela.
articles.summary: Do total negociado, R$ 16,7 bilhões são de responsabilidade da empresa. Após o desconto em multas e juros, a Raízen usará créditos fiscais e pagará R$ 2,5 bilhões à vista para quitar sua parcela.
articles.body:
A Raízen anunciou nesta quarta-feira (28) um acordo com a União para renegociar R$ 22,4 bilhões em dívidas com o governo federal relativas a tributos de empresas do grupo. O acordo, negociado com a Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN) e a Receita Federal, prevê um desconto de R$ 8,5 bilhões em multas e juros sobre a parte da dívida que cabe à companhia pagar.

Do total negociado, cabe à Raízen arcar com R$ 16,7 bilhões. Os outros R$ 5,7 bilhões ficam, em última instância, sob a responsabilidade dos acionistas que controlam a companhia, conforme as regras aplicáveis.

Com os descontos, a parte da dívida que cabe à Raízen cai de R$ 16,7 bilhões para R$ 8,2 bilhões. Para quitar esse valor, a empresa utilizará R$ 5,7 bilhões em créditos fiscais ligados a prejuízos acumulados e pagará os R$ 2,5 bilhões restantes à vista.

🔎 Prejuízos fiscais são perdas apuradas no cálculo dos tributos. Dentro das regras previstas em lei, essas perdas podem ser usadas para reduzir o valor dos impostos a pagar. Nesse caso, a Raízen usará créditos ligados a esses prejuízos para quitar parte da dívida negociada, em vez de pagar todo o valor em dinheiro.

O comunicado não detalha como será paga a parte da dívida que cabe aos acionistas controladores, também de R$ 5,7 bilhões. Apesar de os valores serem iguais, essa parcela é diferente dos créditos fiscais que a Raízen utilizará para pagar parte de sua própria dívida.

Acordo faz parte da reorganização das finanças da Raízen

O acordo com a União faz parte da reorganização das finanças da Raízen, que enfrenta dificuldades para administrar suas dívidas. Segundo a empresa - assessorada pela Alvarez e Marsal, Bichara Advogados e Demarest Advogados - concluir essa negociação é uma das condições para colocar o plano de reestruturação em prática.

Em março, a companhia pediu recuperação extrajudicial para renegociar cerca de R$ 65,1 bilhões em dívidas financeiras, além de valores devidos entre empresas do próprio grupo.

Em julho, a Justiça de São Paulo aprovou o plano , que prevê a renegociação de aproximadamente R$ 61,4 bilhões com bancos e investidores.

🔎 A recuperação extrajudicial permite que uma empresa negocie diretamente com seus credores os prazos e as formas de pagamento das dívidas. Quando o plano obtém o apoio mínimo exigido por lei e é aprovado pela Justiça, suas condições passam a valer também para os credores incluídos na negociação que não aceitaram o acordo individualmente.

No caso da Raízen, o plano também prevê a possibilidade de trocar parte das dívidas por participação na empresa, obter novos recursos com um aumento de capital e vender bens e negócios. O acordo sobre tributos inclui nesse processo a negociação de dívidas com o governo federal.

👉 São negociações diferentes: a recuperação extrajudicial trata das dívidas financeiras com credores; o acordo com a União define as condições para pagar as dívidas relativas a tributos incluídas na negociação.

Dívida elevada e prejuízo pressionam as contas

A situação financeira da Raízen piorou nos últimos anos com a combinação de investimentos elevados, problemas climáticos que prejudicaram as safras de cana-de-açúcar e variações nos preços do açúcar. Os juros altos também aumentaram o custo das dívidas.

No fim de dezembro de 2025, a dívida líquida da companhia chegou a R$ 55,3 bilhões. No terceiro trimestre da safra 2025/26, encerrado no mesmo mês, a empresa registrou prejuízo de R$ 15,6 bilhões.

Do prejuízo total, R$ 11,1 bilhões vieram de uma redução no valor de parte dos bens e direitos da companhia registrada no balanço. Sem esse ajuste contábil, o prejuízo teria sido de aproximadamente R$ 4,5 bilhões.

articles.title: Fed mantém juros dos EUA na faixa de 3,75% a 4% ao ano a poucos dias das eleições para o Congresso | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão vem após alta de 0,25 ponto percentual em setembro, enquanto a disparada do petróleo aumenta as preocupações do BC americano com a inflação.
articles.summary: Decisão vem após alta de 0,25 ponto percentual em setembro, enquanto a disparada do petróleo aumenta as preocupações do BC americano com a inflação.
articles.body:
Prédio do Federal Reserve dos EUA em Washington, EUA (maio/2020) — Foto: Kevin Lamarque / Reuters

O Federal Reserve ( Fed ), banco central dos Estados Unidos, manteve a taxa de juros do país inalterada na faixa de 3,75% a 4% ao ano — maior nível desde outubro de 2025. A decisão, anunciada nesta quarta-feira (28), veio em linha com as expectativas do mercado financeiro.

Na reunião anterior, em setembro , o Fed havia elevado os juros em 0,25 ponto percentual, na primeira alta em mais de três anos. Desde então, a disparada do petróleo em meio às tensões no Oriente Médio tem mantido as preocupações com a inflação no radar do BC americano.

A decisão desta quarta ocorre a poucos dias das eleições de meio de mandato, em 3 de novembro, que definirão o controle do Congresso dos EUA . O pleito acontece em meio à insatisfação dos americanos com a economia e o alto custo de vida, que têm pressionado o governo de Donald Trump . (leia abaixo)

Em comunicado, o Comitê Federal de Mercado Aberto (Fomc) afirmou que a atividade econômica dos EUA segue se expandindo em ritmo forte e que “os gastos domésticos têm se mostrado resilientes”, embora a incerteza permaneça elevada, "em parte, devido a acontecimentos geopolíticos".

Segundo o comitê, a decisão de manter a taxa básica de juros dos EUA inalterada — e em nível historicamente elevado — considera o duplo mandato do Fed: controlar a inflação e promover o máximo emprego. O colegiado destacou ainda que novos dados econômicos ajudarão a orientar as próximas decisões.

➡️ A política de juros nos EUA tem reflexos no Brasil. Com as taxas americanas ainda em níveis altos, cresce a pressão para que a Selic, taxa básica de juros brasileira, permaneça em patamar alto por mais tempo, além de gerar efeitos sobre o câmbio. (leia mais abaixo)

Taxa básica de juros dos EUA - outubro de 2026. — Foto: Arte/g1

Essa foi a 15ª decisão desde que Donald Trump assumiu como 47º presidente dos EUA , em 20 de janeiro de 2025. Desde então, os juros foram reduzidos quatro vezes , mas voltaram a subir na reunião de setembro, em meio a um cenário de incerteza marcado por conflitos geopolíticos, como a guerra entre EUA e Irã , e pela guerra tarifária promovida pelo republicano .

Foi também a quarta reunião sob o comando de Kevin Warsh, indicado por Trump para presidir o banco central dos EUA. Warsh tomou posse em 22 de maio e iniciou oficialmente seu mandato de quatro anos em uma cerimônia na Casa Branca .

A troca de comando no Fed ocorreu após meses de atritos entre Trump e o ex-presidente da instituição, Jerome Powell . Desde o início de seu segundo mandato, o republicano critica os juros elevados e defende cortes nas taxas para evitar que o crédito mais caro prejudique a economia.

Em entrevista coletiva após a decisão, o presidente do Fed, Kevin Warsh, reforçou o compromisso do banco central de levar a inflação de volta à meta de 2% e disse que ainda é preciso avaliar os próximos dados antes de definir novos passos.

Questionado sobre por que o Fed não elevou os juros agora, diante da possibilidade de uma nova alta em dezembro, Warsh afirmou que o combate à inflação não depende de uma data específica nem de um único indicador.

“Controlar a inflação não é uma questão de escolher uma data específica no calendário. Da mesma forma, não se trata de um dado isolado”, afirmou.

Warsh disse que vê sinais positivos nas expectativas de inflação e que os próximos dados ajudarão o Fed a definir o rumo da política monetária. “Há muita coisa acontecendo no mundo, e meus colegas e eu estamos atentos a isso.”

O presidente do Fed reconheceu, porém, que o objetivo ainda não foi alcançado. “Ainda não alcançamos a estabilidade dos preços, mas estamos trabalhando para isso”, disse.

Warsh também afirmou que a economia americana deve ter crescido a um ritmo anualizado superior a 3% no terceiro trimestre , após avanço de 2,4% no segundo trimestre, revisado de 1,8%. Os dados oficiais serão divulgados na quinta-feira (29).

“O terceiro trimestre parece ter registrado uma expansão ainda mais rápida, impulsionada por um consumo saudável, que provavelmente cresceu a uma taxa superior a 3%, e pelos investimentos empresariais, que provavelmente aumentaram a uma taxa de dois dígitos”, afirmou.

O presidente do Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, discursa durante cerimônia de posse no Salão Leste da Casa Branca, em Washington, em 22 de maio de 2026. Foto de arquivo. — Foto: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein

Donald Trump costuma pressionar o Fed por juros mais baixos, mas a inflação continua limitando o espaço para cortes. O índice de preços ao consumidor (CPI) acelerou para 3,7% em 12 meses até setembro, acima da meta de 2% perseguida pelo BC americano.

A alta dos preços também entra no cálculo político às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato, as chamadas “midterms”, marcadas para a próxima terça-feira (3). O pleito vai renovar todas as cadeiras da Câmara e cerca de um terço do Senado .

Os republicanos tentam manter o controle das duas Casas, e perder a maioria em qualquer uma delas pode dificultar a agenda de Trump nos dois últimos anos de mandato.

Levantamentos recentes ajudam a dimensionar o desgaste de Trump relacionado ao tema. Segundo pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos divulgada na segunda-feira (26), 32% aprovam seu governo, enquanto 73% dizem que o custo de vida está caminhando na direção errada.

Ao justificar a decisão desta quarta-feira, o comitê do Fed destacou que a produtividade da economia americana segue crescendo em ritmo forte.

"Os ganhos de empregos têm acompanhado o ritmo de crescimento da força de trabalho, e a taxa de desemprego pouco mudou", afirmou o colegiado.

Em setembro, os EUA criaram 29 mil vagas, bem abaixo das 133 mil registradas em agosto, enquanto a taxa de desemprego subiu de 4,1% para 4,2%, segundo o Departamento do Trabalho.

O Fomc destacou que a inflação continua elevada e afirmou que os próximos dados da economia ajudarão a definir os rumos da política de juros, com o objetivo de levar a inflação à meta de 2%.

A decisão desta quarta-feira não foi unânime. A diretora do Fed Lisa Cook e a presidente do Federal Reserve de Cleveland, Beth Hammack, votaram contra a manutenção dos juros e defenderam uma elevação de 0,25 ponto percentual.

Efeito dos juros no Brasil — e nos mercados

Juros em níveis elevados nos EUA mantêm os títulos públicos americanos, conhecidos como Treasuries, mais atrativos para investidores por oferecerem retornos maiores.

Por serem considerados os investimentos mais seguros do mundo, as Treasuries com rentabilidades elevadas despertam o interesse de investidores estrangeiros, que direcionam recursos aos EUA e fortalecem o dólar.

🔎 Em outra perspectiva: apesar de diversas variáveis interferirem nessa lógica, o movimento tende a reduzir o volume de investimentos estrangeiros no Brasil, desvalorizando o real em relação à moeda americana.

Além disso, o dólar em nível elevado aumenta a pressão sobre a inflação por aqui, com reflexos na manutenção de juros altos pelo Comitê de Política Monetária ( Copom ), do Banco Central do Brasil .

articles.title: Reforma tributária: TCU propôs alíquota de 11,3% para o imposto federal sobre consumo; veja o que muda para empresas em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Para calcular valor da CBS, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com os impostos que estão sendo extintos. Uma das premissas da reforma sobre o consumo é manter atual patamar da carga tributária.
articles.summary: Para calcular valor da CBS, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com os impostos que estão sendo extintos. Uma das premissas da reforma sobre o consumo é manter atual patamar da carga tributária.
articles.body:
O Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) aprovou nesta quarta-feira (28) uma proposta para que a alíquota de referência da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), novo tributo aprovado no âmbito da reforma tributária sobre o consumo, seja de 11,3% em 2027.

O valor será encaminhado ao Congresso Nacional , que poderá concordar ou não . Caberá ao Senado fixar o valor final da alíquota, que será cobrada a partir de 2027, até 15 de dezembro.

Além da CBS, haverá a cobrança transitória do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) com uma alíquota total de 0,1% em 2027 e 2028, dividida entre estados (0,05%) e municípios (0,05%). Essa alíquota começa a subir gradualmente a partir de 2029 .

▶️Para calcular o valor da CBS, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com os impostos que serão extintos no fim de 2026. Isso porque uma das premissas da reforma sobre o consumo é manter o atual patamar da carga tributária.

🔎A CBS substituirá o Programa de Integração Social (PIS), a Contribuição para Financiamento da Seguridade Social (Cofins) e, também, uma parte do Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI).

🔎PIS e Cofins serão extintos em 2026, enquanto o IPI permanecerá somente para itens produzidos na Zona Franca de Manaus (ZFM) — mas com tributação efetiva somente no resto do país.

Com a reforma tributária, os tributos sobre o consumo passarão a seguir o modelo de Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (IVA), adotado em grande parte do mundo, com cobrança não cumulativa.

Isso significa que o imposto será recolhido em cada etapa da cadeia produtiva, mas as empresas poderão descontar os tributos pagos nas fases anteriores .

Por exemplo: se o IVA for de 20%, um produto vendido ao consumidor final por R$ 100 terá imposto, que, ao final da cadeia, totalizará R$ 20, após os mecanismos de crédito e compensação entre os diferentes empresas da produção e comercialização.

Esse sistema não cumulativo será obrigatório nas empresas que realizam vendas de produtos e serviços para outras empresas (o business to business) do lucro real e presumido.

O modelo não cumulativo, porém, não será obrigatório para as empresas do Simples Nacional , que poderão optar por permanecer no regime tradicional ("Simples puro") ou migrar para o modelo híbrido, aproveitando créditos dos tributos recolhidos nas etapas anteriores da cadeia.

Os microempreendedores individuais (MEIs) e os nanoempreendedores , por sua vez, não terão essa opção. Eles permanecerão obrigatoriamente no Simples puro , pois atuam predominantemente em operações destinadas ao consumidor final.

➡️A Receita Federal lembrou que, em 2026, as empresas já estão preenchendo nas notas fiscais eletrônicas os campos referentes aos novos tributos sobre o consumo , em uma fase de testes com alíquotas simbólicas, sem cobrança efetiva.

➡️A partir de 2027, todas as empresas deverão preencher obrigatoriamente os campos relativos aos novos tributos sobre o consumo nas notas fiscais eletrônicas , com exceção dos MEIs nas vendas para pessoas físicas e dos nanoempreendedores.

De acordo com a Receita Federal, o chamado "split payment" da reforma tributária sobre o consumo deverá se tornar obrigatório somente a partir de 2028 nas operações entre empresas .

💵O "split payment" é um dos módulos do super sistema da Receita Federal que foi criado para viabilizar o pagamento dos tributos sobre o consumo em tempo real para o governo, estados e municípios — reduzindo a sonegação fiscal.

🔎Esse sistema também permitirá o ressarcimento quase automático de créditos tributários utilizados na cadeia anterior da produção, um dos pilares da reforma tributária. A ideia é que isso possa ser feito no mesmo dia, em horas.

➡️Na ausência do "split payment" obrigatório a partir do início de 2027, a Receita Federal explicou que as empresas continuarão emitindo, normalmente, as notas fiscais por cada compra e venda .

Ao fim do mês, as empresas emitirão um documento de arrecadação (Darf) para pagar os tributos devidos , como é feito atualmente.

Depois de pagar os tributos, o ressarcimento relativo ao imposto de outras partes da cadeia de produção será creditado em, no máximo dois meses . Isso porque o tributo vence no último dia útil do mês seguinte.

➡️O Fisco informou, porém, que há um modelo alternativo para receber mais rapidamente os créditos tributários, chamado de "Recolhimento pelo Adquirente (RAD)".

Nesse formato, a empresa compradora de um produto ou serviço recolhe diretamente o valor dos tributos da operação e, por isso, consegue obter o crédito tributário de forma mais rápida. A companhia vendedora, por sua vez, recebe o valor da venda já descontado o imposto.

por meio do recolhimento normal, no fim do mês, e abatimento posterior pelo ressarcimento de tributos em outras fases da cadeia;

pelo sistema do recolhimento pelo adquirente, com ressarcimento mais ágil;

pelo "split payment", assim que for gradualmente implementado ao longo de 2027, com ressarcimento imediato de créditos.

As empresas optantes pelo Simples Nacional, exceto os MEIs e os nanoempreendedores, têm até 30 de outubro para escolher o modelo híbrido de recolhimento dos novos tributos sobre o consumo. Essa opção poderá ser cancelada até 20 de dezembro.

Ao optar por esse modelo, a empresa permanece no Simples Nacional para os demais tributos, mas passa a recolher a Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS) e o Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS), os novos tributos sobre o consumo criados pela reforma tributária.

Com isso, a empresa pode aproveitar créditos desses tributos sobre suas compras e também transferir créditos para empresas que adquirirem seus produtos ou serviços.

As empresas do Simples Nacional, sem contar micro e nanoempreendedores, também podem optar por permanecer no regime tradicional do Simples, no qual, geralmente, não se aproveita créditos dos tributos incidentes nas etapas anteriores da cadeia produtiva nem se transfere créditos tributários a seus clientes na venda de bens ou serviços.

"A empresa do Simples ele vai ter que ver qual é o modelo de negócio dela. É uma empresa que quase só vende direto para o consumidor final? Mantém o Simples puro que vai ser mil vezes mais fácil para ela. Ela é uma empresa do Simples meio de cadeia? Ou seja, ela compra de alguém e vende pra uma outra empresa que vai fazer para frente" afirmou Juliano Neves, da Receita Federal.

"Aí talvez ela faça sentido pra ela sair do Simples puro e ir para essa situação híbrida, porque aí ela consegue transferir crédito para quem quer estar comprando", acrescentou.

➡️Dados da Receita Federal indicam que o Simples Nacional concentrava 7,35 milhões de empresas, sem contar MEIs e nanoempreendedores, no fim de 2025, o equivalente a 28,6% do total de empresas ativas no país.

Juliano Neves, que é subsecretário da Receita Federal, observou que a maior parte das empresas do Simples Nacional faz justamente vendas direto ao consumidor final, não sendo necessário, nesse caso, optar pelo sistema híbrido (que permite transferência de créditos).

Empresas começam 2026 com o desafio de se adaptarem às novas regras da reforma tributária — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

articles.title: Bolsa brasileira fecha em queda pelo 3º dia seguido | G1
articles.standfirst: Os investidores ainda reagem ao resultado da eleição e esperam sinais mais claros sobre como o governo pretende controlar os gastos e a dívida pública, além da definição da nova equipe econômica.
articles.summary: Os investidores ainda reagem ao resultado da eleição e esperam sinais mais claros sobre como o governo pretende controlar os gastos e a dívida pública, além da definição da nova equipe econômica.
articles.body:
A bolsa de valores caiu nesta quarta-feira (28) pelo terceiro dia seguido.

O Ibovespa fechou em queda de 2,68%, aos 171 mil pontos. Os investidores ainda reagem ao resultado da eleição e esperam sinais mais claros sobre como o governo pretende controlar os gastos e a dívida pública, além da definição da nova equipe econômica.

Bolsa brasileira fecha em queda pelo 3º dia seguido — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Em entrevista ao GloboNews Mais , o chefe do Centro de Estudos Monetários do FGV/Ibre, José Júlio Senna, diz que o governo precisa agir rápido e anunciar um nome de peso:

“Seria importante que o governo viesse com uma decisão muito firme, indicando o responsável pela Fazenda. Aquilo que o Brasil mais precisa hoje é um choque de expectativas favorável. Estabilidade macroeconômica é uma pré-condição para o crescimento econômico. Não há registro na história de país que consiga se desenvolver com instabilidade macroeconômica - inflação para cima, juros altos demais e dívida saindo de controle, e assim por diante. Então, eu acho que o primeiro grande passo seria anunciar um nome, mas um nome de fato de peso. Uma pessoa que conheça os futuros potenciais parceiros, saiba montar uma equipe competente para virar esse jogo”.

Uma notícia sobre juros nos Estados Unidos também influenciou o mercado financeiro nesta quarta-feira (28). A taxa básica lá se manteve entre 3,75% e 4% ao ano. Foram dez votos pela manutenção e dois pelo aumento dos juros. O Banco Central americano está preocupado com o aumento do custo de vida.

No Brasil, o dólar teve uma pequena queda, recuou para R$ 5,34.

articles.title: IR 2026: Mais de 500 contribuintes do Acre têm direito a lote residual | G1
articles.standfirst: Consulta foi liberada no dia 23. Recurso totaliza mais de R$ 1,4 milhão. A consulta pode ser feita no site da Receita Federal informando o CPF e data de nascimento.
articles.summary: Consulta foi liberada no dia 23. Recurso totaliza mais de R$ 1,4 milhão. A consulta pode ser feita no site da Receita Federal informando o CPF e data de nascimento.
articles.body:
O Imposto de Renda da Pessoa Física (IRPF) 2026 vai pagar R$ 1.428.345,88 distribuídos entre 560 contribuintes do Acre nesta sexta-feira (30). A consulta está disponível desde o dia 23 de outubro.

Segundo o órgão, a maioria é formada por aqueles que não têm prioridade no recebimento. O lote contempla também restituições residuais de exercícios anteriores.

Para descobrir se você vai receber, basta acessar o menu 'Meu Imposto de Renda' no site da Receita Federal. É necessário ter em mãos o número do CPF, a data de nascimento e selecionar a opção do exercício 2026 do imposto de renda.

Na 2ª Região Fiscal, composta pelo Acre, Rondônia, Pará, Amapá, Amazonas e Roraima, deve ser pago R$ 25.288.041,69 para 10.677 contribuintes.

Lote residual será pago nesta sexta-feira (30) — Foto: g1

📲 Como saber se a restituição está disponível?

Para saber se a restituição está disponível, o contribuinte deve acessar o site da Receita Federal , clicar em "Meu Imposto de Renda" e, em seguida, em "Consultar a Restituição" .

Se identificar alguma pendência na declaração, o contribuinte pode corrigir as informações prestadas.

A página traz orientações e canais de prestação do serviço, permitindo consulta da situação da declaração.

A Receita disponibiliza, ainda, aplicativo para tablets e smartphones que possibilita consultar diretamente nas bases da Receita Federal informações sobre liberação das restituições do IRPF e a situação cadastral de uma inscrição no CPF.

🤑 Como o pagamento da restituição é feito?

Restituição pode ser conferida no site da Receita — Foto: Nubia Pacheco/G1

O pagamento da restituição é feito na conta bancária informada no momento da declaração do Imposto de Renda, de forma direta ou por PIX.

Se, por algum motivo, o crédito não for realizado (por exemplo, a conta informada foi desativada), a Receita afirma que os valores ficarão disponíveis para resgate por até um ano no Banco do Brasil.

Neste caso, o cidadão poderá reagendar o crédito dos valores de pelo Portal BB , ou ligando para a Central de Relacionamento BB:

0800-729-0088 (telefone especial exclusivo para deficientes auditivos).

Conforme a Receita Federal, caso o contribuinte não resgate o valor da restituição no prazo de um ano, para retirar o dinheiro depois disso, deverá fazer um pedido no Portal e-CAC .

Acesse o menu Declarações e Demonstrativos > Meu Imposto de Renda e clique em "Solicitar restituição não resgatada na rede bancária" .

articles.title: Trump DOE loans $5B to nuclear plants that will power data centers
articles.summary: Constellation Energy will get $5 billion in government loans to modernize nuclear reactors. Most of the new capacity is already committed to Google, Amazon,...
articles.body:
The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts.

Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon.

Constellation said it plans to use the financing to "uprate" 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels.

The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, "could lower financing costs" for the projects, Constellation said in a press release .

The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick).

Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois.

On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting "affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses," though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation's announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government's claim to TechCrunch.

Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end.

By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy's loans could boost Constellation's bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both.

articles.title: People really, really hate the 'Liberty Biberty' mascot. Maybe that's good for Liberty Mutual?
articles.summary: A protest in Boston outside the Liberty Mutual office over the mascot shows how deep the hate goes.
articles.body:
"Liberty Biberty" is a much-hated new yellow puppet mascot for Liberty Mutual, appearing in ads.

People are so riled up that there was a protest at its Boston HQ. Its organizer called the mascot "a disgusting little creature."

But this kind of cheeky "hate" might actually work in Liberty's favor, an ad expert says.

On Sunday, a small crowd took to the streets of Boston to protest, holding signs, chanting, with one person even appearing in full costume and face paint. The protest took place in front of the Back Bay headquarters of insurance company Liberty Mutual . The protest was not against some sort of corporate malfeasance, political, or even a social justice issue.

They were protesting the existence of Liberty Biberty, the new fuzzy yellow mascot that appears in the insurance giant's TV ads.

People, for some reason, really hate the Liberty Biberty puppet.

There's a Facebook page with over 40,000 people devoted to hating it. There's TikToks. Reddit threads. I even saw a ghastly tattoo depicting the spherical character being fed into a meat grinder. John Oliver did a segment about it on HBO's "Last Week Tonight" recently.

The concept of the ads is surreal and self-referential. Liberty Biberty is a yellow puppet who has appeared in a few TV ads so far. In one, he appears on someone's car and tells them about the benefits of auto insurance, and then is carried off by a hawk. In another, he chats to a bored bartender, and then meets the aforementioned hunky actor prone to malapropisms.

Liberty Mutual is well aware of the, ahem, passionate response.

"We're encouraged by how strongly people are engaging with him, whether they love him or feel differently," Jenna Lebel, Liberty Mutual's chief marketing officer for US retail markets, told Business Insider. "We've been encouraged by the early results, including independent testing that shows Biberty performing above average on attention and brand attribution."

Insurance companies' advertising strategies for the last decade or more has been focused on a series of recognizable characters like Flo from Progressive, Jake from State Farm, and "Mayhem" from Allstate. Let us not forget the forefather of them all, the Geico gecko. Liberty Mutual has also had Doug and the LiMu Emu, as well as a hunky actor prone to malapropisms — hence "biberty." (Don't worry: Doug and the LiMu Emu are still active, Liberty Mutual's PR person assured me. Some complaints about Biberty were that people thought it had replaced the popular human/avian duo.)

articles.title: What the Fed's interest rate decision means for your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
articles.summary: Here's how the Fed's rate decision could impact savings products, various types of loans, and credit cards.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

The Federal Reserve left short-term interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, following September's first hike in more than three years. Based on 30-day fed funds futures prices , Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee are likely to raise the benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point in December.

"The Federal Reserve's interest rate decision takes center stage this week after a hotter-than-expected September CPI report showed price pressures broadening," Ehsan Khoman, economist with the BlackRock Investment Institute, said in an analysis. "We don't view recent tightening as the start of a sustained hiking cycle."

What will a higher rate environment mean for your money? The federal funds rate influences not only the stock market, but also savings rates, interest charges, and, to a lesser degree, mortgage rates. Here's how to prepare for the impact on your deposits, credit, and debt.

How a Fed rate hike affects checking and savings accounts

A series of Fed rate hikes will likely slowly lift deposit earnings. However, deposit accounts are mostly for convenience, not substantial returns. So far in 2026, the gains have been meager.

Your checking account churns cash flow to pay bills. The liquidity limits your earning power.

The national average interest rate on checking accounts has barely budged this year, remaining at 0.07%. A Fed short-term interest rate increase may nudge earnings incrementally higher.

Interest rates on savings accounts are only marginally better, clinging to 0.38%. But savings accounts are for near-term money.

High-yield savings accounts have been more effective at paying interest. Rates are split in the 3% to 4% range.

This is one category where rate shopping and subsequent increases in the Fed rate really pay off.

If you have $10,000 or more that you want to keep on the sidelines but easy to tap when you need it, money market accounts have been convenient — but low-paying, with a national average payout of only 0.63%.

A high-yield money market account is a better option, where you may still find a rate just under 4%, but mostly in the mid-3% range.

CD rates have begun inching higher. The national average on a 12-month CD is 1.76%, but you can find better deals if you're willing to shop around — and move your money to the best offer.

Your minimum deposit and term will affect your rate. Fed rate hikes may ultimately sweeten CD rates.

What a rate hike will mean for mortgages

And then there are mortgage rates , often the largest borrowing expense consumers face. Fed interest rate increases don't usually affect mortgage rates — the bond market often prices in hikes before monetary policy moves.

At the end of February and into early March, mortgage rates were hitting three-year lows. Then the war in the Middle East began, and rather than falling further, home loan rates reversed course and edged higher. Home loan rates have recently topped 7% (depending on the rate reporting source), mirroring the higher yields of the 10-year Treasury note .

Housing industry analysts at the Mortgage Bankers Association and Fannie Mae predict that mortgage rates will remain near 7.5% through 2027.

What a rate hike means for personal loans and student loans

Personal loan interest rates have risen slightly to an average of 11.9%. Advertised personal loan rates vary widely, from 6% to 9%.

The Federal Reserve influences consumer loan rates by setting the federal funds rate, which affects how much banks charge each other for overnight lending. That cost typically gets passed on to borrowers through higher or lower rates on personal, auto, and student loans.

The Federal Reserve doesn't set student loan rates directly, but its federal funds rate influences the 10-year Treasury yield (which determines federal loan rates) and the prime rate (which determines private loan rates).

The federal funds rate doesn't directly determine federal student loan interest rates, but it can influence them indirectly. Congress sets the federal student loan rates based on the 10-year Treasury note, adding a fixed margin each year.

But the 10-year Treasury yield moves with investor demand, not the Fed's rate. When investors expect high inflation or strong economic growth, they demand higher yields, which can push federal student loan rates higher.

That said, if the Fed's rate hikes successfully cool inflation, Treasury yields may drop — and the following year's federal student loan rates could be lower.

Private student loans are offered by banks, credit unions, and online lenders, many of which use the prime rate as a basis for setting their interest rates. The prime rate moves alongside the Federal Reserve's rate decisions. So, when the Fed raises rates, new private loan rates usually rise, and when it cuts rates, they tend to fall.

What happens to credit cards when the Fed raises rates

Credit card interest affects everyone — except those who pay off their balance each month. Rates have climbed from around 16% in 2021 to an average of over 22% toda

Michele Raneri, vice president and head of U.S. research at TransUnion, expects consumers to see "minimally higher" borrowing costs as variable-rate credit products reflect the Fed's interest rate hike.

"A consumer carrying the average Q2 2026 credit card balance of $6,610 at a 22% APR could see an increase of $1.38 in minimum monthly payments as those higher rates are passed on," Raneri said in a statement. "While the near-term impact on minimum monthly credit card payments may be relatively small, higher borrowing costs can add up over time, particularly for consumers carrying larger balances or making only minimum payments.

Reducing revolving debt will limit the impact of rising interest rates, she added.

Yahoo Finance tip: The best way to earn a lower credit card interest rate right away is to ask. If you make regular payments and have seen your credit score improving, it's a good time to call your credit card provider and ask for a lower interest rate.

How the Fed's interest rate policy impacts your investments

"There's an old Wall Street adage that says, 'Don't fight the Fed,'" Kevin Gordon, head of macro research and strategy at Schwab, said in an analysis. "The idea behind it was that there's often a lot of turbulence associated with Fed rate-hiking cycles."

He noted that history shows an average maximum loss of more than 10% for the S&P 500 sometime within 12 months after the start of a higher-interest-rate cycle.

"Broadly, though, we would say that the economic backdrop is still relatively favorable for the Fed to be hiking. So even if it is a hiking cycle where they do hike more than once, we think that the economy can probably hold up," he added.

Stock prices often react to the Fed's rate actions, but they are only one of many factors affecting the investing climate and stock prices. AI investments and oil-price-fueled inflation seem to be the most motivating factors for equity markets these days.

If you want to manage your investments for the current environment, monitor broader economic and corporate profit trends, as well as interest rates. If you prefer to stay conservative, fill your portfolio with high-quality stocks that have proven themselves in all economic cycles.

Then, wait patiently for long-term growth.

The Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions can directly impact your wallet. So what's better: high or low interest rates?

articles.title: Oracle Projects $30 Billion Free Cash Flow in Fiscal 2029
articles.summary: Oracle Corp. gave a long-term outlook for free cash flow that was better than analysts’ estimates, easing investor nerves about the potential payoff from its...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Oracle Corp. gave a long-term outlook for free cash flow that was better than analysts' estimates, easing investor nerves about the potential payoff from its artificial intelligence spending.

Free cash flow will be $30 billion in the fiscal year ending in May 2029, Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said Wednesday during the company's annual conference in Las Vegas. Investors had expected free cash flow to remain negative in that year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Oracle, long known for its database software, has been working to refashion itself as a provider of computing power for AI work and is embarking on a major build-out of data centers for OpenAI and other customers. Wall Street is closely watching the scale of spending on these ambitious projects and how quickly Oracle can complete them.

The shares jumped as much as 9.6% on the company's long-range forecast. The stock had dropped 33% this year through Tuesday's close.

articles.title: India’s GitHub developer base hits 32 million, adds 10 million in a year
articles.summary: India’s GitHub community rose to 32 million after adding 10 million developers in a year, ranking second globally behind the US, says Octoverse 2026.
articles.body: Bengaluru: India added 10 million developers to GitHub in the past year, taking its developer community to 32 million, the second-largest globally after the US, according to GitHub’s Octoverse 2026 report.The US remains the largest developer community, with 38.3 million developers, after adding 10.3 million over the year. Together, India and the US account for roughly 31% of GitHub’s more than 225 million developers worldwide.China ranks third with 12.4 million developers, followed by Brazil with 10.2 million, Japan with 7.15 million, the UK with 6.4 million, Indonesia with 6.3 million and Germany with 6.3 million.Brazil added 3.2 million developers during the year, the third-highest increase among countries, while Japan added 2.6 million and Indonesia 1.97 million.Developer numbers and coding activity, however, tell slightly different stories. Based on adjusted pushes to public repositories, the US leads, followed by India, China and Brazil. Germany, the UK, South Korea, France and Japan also feature among the leading countries by this measure. South Korea ranks seventh in coding activity despite not featuring in the top 10 by developer count.GitHub’s latest report also tracks progress against projections it made last year for developer communities in 2030. A year into the projections, every country has covered at least a fifth of the distance towards its target.The US has covered 38.6% of the gap to its projected 54.7 million developers by 2030, while India has covered 28.3% of the distance to its target of 57.5 million. India is still projected to overtake the US by 2030, although the US added slightly more developers in the latest year.Some smaller markets are progressing faster relative to their targets. Morocco has covered 54.4% of the distance to its 2030 projection, followed by Indonesia at 45.4%, Nigeria at 37%, Japan at 36.8% and Germany at 35.2%.China has covered 24.2% of its projected growth, South Africa 23.3% and Kenya 21.7%.The factors driving developer growth vary across regions. In the Americas, fintech and digital payments are important drivers, particularly in Brazil. Europe, the Middle East and Africa are seeing growth linked to AI adoption in manufacturing, startups and expanding developer communities across Africa. In Asia-Pacific, govt investment in AI infrastructure and talent is a common factor.Projecting future growth is becoming more difficult, GitHub said. Of 43 models it ran to estimate developer growth through 2031, 21 projected that developer numbers would more than triple, while 19 projected growth of between two and three times. Only three models projected less than a doubling.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Canada reports limited progress in trade talks with US
articles.summary: OTTAWA, Oct 28 (Reuters) - There has been limited progress in trade talks with the United States to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, a Canadian g...
articles.body:
By Promit Mukherjee and David Shepardson

OTTAWA, Oct 28 (Reuters) - There has been limited progress in trade talks with the United States to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, a Canadian government ‌official with knowledge of the discussions said on Wednesday.

US President Donald Trump widened a trade rift ‌by imposing 50% tariffs on a wide range of imports from Canada in August, accusing the US neighbor to the north of discriminatory treatment ​of American goods. Canada responded with retaliatory tariffs.

Reuters reported on Monday that the two countries were working on a trade deal. Talks on a broader agreement stalled in August when Canada walked away from the negotiating table.

"While discussions have continued, there has been limited progress," the Canadian official told Reuters, speaking on condition of anonymity.

Prime Minister Mark Carney, who on Monday ‌said there had been "a slight intensification" in ⁠talks, reiterated on Wednesday that Canada is ready to sign an agreement that is in the interests of both nations.

"If those deals present themselves, we will pursue them, but we're ⁠not at that position right now," Carney told reporters.

A US government official said on Wednesday there were significant ongoing talks, including between US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Dominic LeBlanc, Canada's minister responsible for trade with the United States.

The White House said ​the ​Office of the US Trade Representative and the Commerce Department are ​continuing to work together on key issues involving ‌trade with Canada, and that both Lutnick and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have had discussions with their Canadian counterparts in recent days.

Trump's Republican Party is fighting to retain control of the US Congress in the November 3 midterm elections. Tariffs on Canadian imports have become a political liability for the US president, with Republican candidates in border states calling for an end to the trade war with Canada.

Some experts have said the Trump administration may be less willing ‌to make trade concessions to Canada after the midterms.

The latest talks ​have focused on tariffs imposed under Section 232 of US trade law, ​including up to a 50% tariff on Canadian ​steel and a 25% tariff on autos. The Commerce Department, which administers the Section 232 ‌tariffs, did not immediately respond to a request for ​comment.

Trump on Sunday said the trade ​dispute would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics.

Trump signed an order last week to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit companies from Maine, where incumbent Republican ​Senator Susan Collins is locked in ‌a tight reelection race. Trump added a number of Canadian products to the 50% tariff list to ​offset the tariff relief provided in his order.

(Reporting by Promit Mukherjee, David Shepardson and David Ljunggren; ​Writing by Caroline StaufferEditing by Tomasz Janowski and Will Dunham)

articles.title: Airbus holds annual targets, bets on year-end delivery surge
articles.summary: Oct 28 (Reuters) - Airbus maintained its full-year forecasts and production plans on Wednesday after reporting mixed third-quarter earnings, leaving investor...
articles.body:
By Gianluca Lo Nostro, Joanna Plucinska and Florence Loeve

Oct 28 (Reuters) - Airbus maintained its full-year forecasts and production plans on Wednesday after reporting mixed third-quarter earnings, leaving investors focused on whether it can hit ‌its annual aircraft-delivery target.

The world's largest planemaker stuck to its target of delivering around 870 aircraft this ‌year, which would be its highest tally ever, and left production goals unchanged. It will need a record fourth quarter to reach that mark.

"Everybody will ​be watching to see if they can get to that 870 number, or whether sometime in December, they need to indicate that they can't get to that number," said Ronan Murphy, a director at Alton Aviation Consultancy. "They must have a view that they can still get close to it."

Airbus said adjusted operating profit reached €1.77 billion ($2 billion) in the three months to end-September, ‌broadly matching the analysts' estimate in a poll ⁠compiled by the company. Revenue fell 2% to €17.47 billion, below the estimate of €17.91 billion.

Airbus' American Depositary Receipts were trading up 1% following its earnings report.

Airbus traditionally delivers more aircraft ⁠in the final months of the year, but has previously been forced to cut delivery targets late in the year as engine shortages and other supply-chain constraints disrupted production.

Airbus says those pressures have recently begun to ease.

"Two years ago we postponed part of ​the ramp-up ​and we progressed at a slower pace towards the ramp-up ​for a number of reasons, including the engines. "We ‌are no longer in that situation," CEO Guillaume Faury told reporters.

The two separate quality flaws detected on some A321neo and A330 jetliners have been identified and contained, with deliveries still flowing, Faury added.

Murphy cautioned that supply-chain pressures had eased but not disappeared.

"The delays have slowed down, but there are still delays from when things were originally," said Murphy.

Free cash flow before customer financing since January was a negative €1.27 billion, reflecting higher inventories as Airbus prepared for a stronger delivery performance ‌later in the year and ramped up production for year-end deliveries.

"We ​are close to the end of October. We have a high level ​of inventory," Faury said, projecting confidence that Airbus will ​meet its delivery target this year.

Rival Boeing highlighted production delays and supply-chain challenges on Tuesday, ‌with CEO Kelly Ortberg saying the US planemaker would ​miss key production and jet ​delivery targets this year.
authors: By Gianluca Lo Nostro, Joanna Plucinska and Florence Loeve

articles.title: The Fed just removed a 2027 rate decision — making the remaining 7 even more important
articles.summary: The latest decision at the Fed raises the stakes of each meeting.
articles.body:
The Warsh Fed's taciturn nature has already raised the stakes for each FOMC meeting. With fewer hints or forward guidance about what the Fed is thinking and planning comes more suspense.

And next year, those stakes will be even higher as the Fed removes a rate decision from its calendar, making each meeting even more important and potentially adding another layer of uncertainty and volatility to markets .

At the October policy meeting on Wednesday, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced this major change to the Fed's calendar and added that 2028 might feature only six rate decisions. The meetings themselves will remain on the calendar, but instead of the Fed debating rates, broader monetary policy topics will be on the agenda.

The Wednesday meeting saw the Fed hold rates steady, but two dissenting governors wanted a hike.

Warsh said the reasoning behind the schedule change is to "reserve the time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons."

We've all been wondering how the newly installed chair would reshape the Fed. Already, he's been doing that by changing the nature of the Fed's public communication.

"I don't believe in forward guidance," Warsh said on Wednesday. His remarks echoed his move earlier this year to end the years-long practice of offering forward guidance — removing an important signal for Wall Street and Main Street alike.

Warsh himself has not contributed a "dot" to the central bank's quarterly chart showing where individual policymakers expect short-term interest rates to go, and he doesn't plan to do so.

Now the Fed will also have fewer decisions to discuss.

articles.title: FedEx Boosts Outlook as Momentum Builds Ahead of Holidays
articles.summary: FedEx Corp. raised its profit and sales guidance for the year, another promising sign for parcel carriers heading into the all-important holiday shipping sea...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- FedEx Corp. raised its profit and sales guidance for the year, another promising sign for parcel carriers heading into the all-important holiday shipping season.

Adjusted earnings will be $18 to $18.60 a share in 2026, up from a prior forecast range topping out at $18.10, FedEx said Wednesday in a statement as it reported quarterly results. The company now sees revenue growth of about 12%.

The improved outlook is a boon for the company's ongoing network overhaul and suggests shipping demand is holding strong heading into the busy year-end months, despite high prices and economic volatility. FedEx echoed rival United Parcel Service Inc., which raised its sales and profit outlook earlier this week.

For the three months ending Sept. 30, FedEx's adjusted earnings rose to $3.74 a share. Its revenue and operating margin improved as well.

While the report was broadly positive, the stock was down in postmarket trading, possibly reflecting confusion around a change in FedEx's reporting calendar that made it difficult to compare with analyst estimates. After a brief drop of 7.1%, the shares pared declines and were trading 1.9% lower as of 4:45 p.m. in New York.

This year has been one of transition for FedEx, which recently spun off its freight division and sold its supply-chain unit to CMA CGM Group, moves to allow FedEx to focus on its core parcel business. It's also progressing through a sweeping overhaul under Chief Executive Officer Raj Subramaniam to merge the historically separate air and ground delivery networks.

The quarter also marked a change in FedEx's reporting schedule as it moved to a fiscal year aligning with the calendar year. The company will now report quarterly results on a similar basis to UPS.

The parcel business has struggled to rebound from several years of stagnant demand, pressured by inflation and tariffs, as well as a comedown from a pandemic-driven boom in e-commerce deliveries. Both FedEx and UPS have shifted their emphasis to high-value shipments, such as those for the healthcare and high-tech sectors.

As of the end of the third quarter, FedEx held $2.7 billion in cash on hand for tariff refunds paid by customers on President Donald Trump's IEEPA tariffs, which were struck down by the Supreme Court earlier this year. FedEx filed a lawsuit in February against the administration seeking refunds, and has said it will distribute the refunds to its customers.

articles.title: Google stock plunges as Q3 sales fall short of expectations
articles.summary: Google reported disappointing Q3 results after the bell Wednesday.
articles.body:
Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) reported its third quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, missing revenue projections on lower-than-anticipated advertising sales, despite Google Cloud growth of 103%.

Google saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.12 on revenue of 127.58 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $3.01 on revenue of $127.93 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs came in at $111.21 billion. Wall Street was anticipating $111.29 billion.

Google's advertising segment saw sales of $82.01 billion versus expectations of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit brought in $30.71 billion. Analysts were projecting revenue of $29.1 billion.

Google stock fell more than 8% on the news.

Google is also burning through its free cash flow, declining from $-5.85 billion in Q2 to -$9.06 billion in Q3.

The results come just hours after the company debuted its latest frontier AI model.

Google said the new model, Gemini 4 Carbon, outpaces even its Gemini 4 Argon, which it released just two weeks ago. The company claimed Carbon also beats out competing models, including OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude Opus 5.5.

According to Google CEO Sundar Pichai, the Gemini app now has more than 1 billion users, making it the fastest-growing app in the company's history.

Investors on Wall Street, meanwhile, have been vacillating between concern and exuberance about the future of AI and whether hyperscalers' vast investments in the technology will pay off.

Those fears came into focus last week as traders dumped CoreWeave stock amid questions about the company's massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.

On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives expressed a bullish take on an otherwise bearish market reaction.

"Cloud doubling on contracted demand with margin expanding at the same time settles the demand side of the capex debate for this quarter, and TPU systems contributing now rather than next year puts a second growth engine on the field the other hyperscalers do not have."

But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta, thanks to its new Muse AI agent . According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.

If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.

"Search usage [and] growth is back in focus given Muse launch and challenges Google could face in migrating users to agentic while maintaining strong monetization," Post wrote.

articles.title: Oil Declines as Traders Parse Signs of Fresh Diplomacy on Iran
articles.summary: Oil dropped as traders weighed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Oil dropped as traders weighed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran.

West Texas Intermediate fell toward $102 a barrel, after rising almost 3% in the previous session, while Brent closed near $115. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran continued to give diplomacy chance, and the Wall Street Journal reported US Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the nation's top security body.

President Donald Trump told Axios on Wednesday that negotiations were taking place through mediators but stressed he didn't know whether they would bear fruit. "We need to finish the job — either through a deal or another way — we will find out if negotiations can succeed," he was quoted as saying.

Global crude benchmark Brent has rallied by 11% this month, touching the highest since April, as the conflict dragged on. The surge has heaped pressure on consumers and presented a challenge to central bankers seeking to contain inflation. While the Federal Reserve opted to keep policy unchanged this week, traders expect officials to resume tightening in December.

US voters will go to the polls on Nov. 3 for midterm elections amid signs that there'll be a slump in support for Republicans. President Trump has given frequent signals that he may opt to resume a military campaign against Tehran after ballots have been cast, possibly in coordination with Israel's forces.

In Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu edged ahead of opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot after a tightly fought election, although neither has a clear path toward forming a government. It will be days before President Isaac Herzog chooses who gets the chance to cobble together a new ruling coalition.

articles.title: Intel to report Q3 earnings as chip stocks continue to rebound
articles.summary: Intel will report its Q3 earnings after the bell Thursday.
articles.body:
Computer processor maker Intel ( INTC ) will report its third-quarter earnings after the bell Thursday, as chip stocks continue to recover from an AI-driven rout over the last month.

Intel shares fell more than 20% over the last month, while Micron ( MU ) and AMD ( AMD ) have dropped roughly 10%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) is off about 3%.

The earnings report comes after memory chip maker SK Hynix ( SKHY ) reported strong results with revenue skyrocketing 328% to some $78.7 billion, with operating profit jumping 632%, helping to ease concerns about the AI trade.

For the quarter, Intel is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $0.40 on revenue of $16.5 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. The company reported EPS of $0.23 and revenue of $13.6 billion in the same period last year.

Intel's Intel Product segment, which includes sales of its data center and PC processors, is expected to come in at $15.5 billion, with PC chip sales coming in at $8.8 billion. Data center sales are projected to be $6.6 billion.

AI is driving strong demand for Intel's data center central processing units (CPUs), prompting the company to increase its capital expenditures as it looks to build more manufacturing facilities to meet customer demand.

At the same time, the PC industry is struggling as memory and storage price spikes force companies to raise laptop and desktop prices, lowering overall sales volume but raising average selling prices.

Intel's Foundry business, its chip manufacturing arm, is expected to generate $6.1 billion in revenue, a potential 44% year-over-year increase.

Intel's foundry business is reportedly beginning to sign big-name customers, with The Information reporting that Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) placed an order with the company to produce 3 million of its custom Tensor Processing Units. Nvidia is also reportedly in talks with Intel to build its chips.

According to Reuters , Intel is also in discussions with SK Hynix about a deal that could see the memory chip maker lease space at Intel's Ohio manufacturing facility.

articles.body:
Seemingly, everyone is digging into Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO prospectus this week, even other C-suite execs like Robinhood ( HOOD ) CFO Shiv Verma.

"I have gone through it. The growth rates are pretty incredible, … up 1,300% year over year, I can't recall seeing another company doing that well," Verma said on Yahoo Finance about what caught his attention from the prospectus.

"The other thing I thought was interesting is they were showing what percentage of their customers are in different buckets," Verma added. "And so if you spend more than $10 million a year, you're a top 250 customer. I thought that was a pretty interesting stat, as I thought it'd be a little bit larger, but it just goes to show you how big their future TAM [total addressable market] is."

Verma has no choice but to read every single page of the S-1 for at least two reasons.

For one, Verma runs point on Robinhood Ventures.

It's a concentrated investment portfolio heavily anchored in premier AI and data infrastructure giants, including OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), Databricks ( DATB.PVT ), the AI-hiring platform Mercor, and the coding assistant Cognition. So how Anthropic is received by investors could greatly impact the valuations of the companies in the portfolio and, by extension, the overall value of Robinhood.

Secondly, there will likely be a lot of interest from Robinhood's retail investor base, enthralled with all things AI, in trading Anthropic shares and also to use the hotly anticipated debut to scale in and out of other AI names.

Anthropic publicly files IPO prospectus, noting strong revenue growth and massive spending

When is the Anthropic IPO? The stock could start trading as soon as Nov. 16.

5 unexpected risk factors Anthropic is worried about

As it stands, the S-1 has been generally well received by markets.

Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, the prospectus showed. The filing also discloses an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, a strong signal of aggressive AI spending in the years ahead.

On an adjusted basis, Anthropic posted $1.62 billion in operating income through the first six months of 2026 compared to a loss of $1.85 billion last year.

The company is winning praise for its strong top-line growth rates and more than $131 billion in cash on hand.

Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.

Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

articles.title: Law firm that handled Lehman, Enron bankruptcies plans to wind down
articles.summary: Leaders at Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the nearly century-old law firm that worked for companies from the Lehman Brothers to General Motors, recommended on Wednesday that the firm shut down.
articles.body: Leaders at Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the nearly century-old law firm that worked for companies from the Lehman Brothers to General Motors, recommended on Wednesday that the firm shut down. “Following a careful review of strategic alternatives, the Firm’s Management Committee has recommended to the partnership that the Firm pursue an orderly wind-down,” a Weil spokesperson said in a statement Wednesday. The firm’s partners are expected to vote on the recommendation “in the coming days,” according to the statement. Equity partners hold stakes in law firms and can vote on company matters. For over 90 years, the law firm was well-known through Wall Street for steering high-profile corporate litigation such as bankruptcies and mergers. Weil advised the Lehman Brothers during the 2008 financial crisis, and the firm claims it brought General Motors out of bankruptcy in “just 40 days.” The firm said it guided debtors such as Enron, whose 2001 bankruptcy filing was the largest in American history at the time. It also advised Microsoft’s $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard as well as AT&T’s acquisition of DirecTV. The firm had been mired by an exodus of prominent partners, largely driven by competition from rivals, legal news outlet Law.com earlier reported. And a potential merger with another law firm, Willkie Farr, fell through this year. Weil is announcing its closure without filing for bankruptcy. The news sent shockwaves through the Big Law industry, which has been going through its own changes. Big mergers and acquisitions have led to more competition for top talent – and then there’s the looming dread of artificial intelligence. Weil was founded in 1931 and employs approximately 1,200 lawyers in offices from New York to Munich to Hong Kong, according to its website. The firm did not announce plans for its employees or office spaces on Wednesday.

articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Fed holds rate steady ahead of midterms Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. © Mark Schiefelbein, Associated Press The central bank’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the…
articles.body:
Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation.

The central bank’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent .

“The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal,” Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC’s statement.

Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland’s president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady.

Wednesday’s decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point, the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war, creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle.

Warsh said Wednesday he has “started to see some changes” in financial and credit conditions since the Fed raised rates in September.

“They have tightened for some businesses and households , much as we would expect,” he added. “Market participants are becoming somewhat more discerning in their capital allocations.”

But the Fed chair noted he was “unwilling and unable” to call financial conditions “tight,” while arguing they are headed “in the direction of achieving a longer or durable period of economic growth and price stability.”

Traders were overwhelming anticipating a hold, pricing in a 92.8 percent chance of the FOMC keeping rates steady as Wednesday afternoon, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

articles.title: On debut, Jio 2nd most valuable company, behind only parent Reliance Industries
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Jio Platforms, the telecoms-to-technology arm of the RIL group, had a blockbuster listing on Wednesday, becoming the second most valued company in
articles.body: MUMBAI: Jio Platforms, the telecoms-to-technology arm of the RIL group, had a blockbuster listing on Wednesday, becoming the second most valued company in India and the fifth most valued telecom services provider in the world, on debut.The stock listed at Rs 1,358, a 21% premium over its initial public offering price of Rs 1,119, and rallied to close the session at Rs 1,419, up 27%. This gave the company a market capitalisation of Rs 13.1 lakh crore, putting it behind only its parent Reliance Industries (Rs 15.7 lakh crore) but ahead of its peer Bharti Airtel (Rs 12.2 lakh crore), exchange data showed. It’s only the second time in Indian corporate history that the two most valuable companies are from the same group. In the late 1980s and 1990s, Tata Steel and Tata Motors (then Tisco and Telco) were consistently the two top companies by market cap on BSE.At 30.3L cr m-cap, RIL group most valued nowAhead of its listing on NSE, where four generations of the Ambani family were present, Jio Platforms director Isha Ambani recalled that nearly half a century ago, RIL had gone public through its Rs 2.8-crore IPO, at a valuation of Rs 10 crore. Dhirubhai Ambani, her grandfather, had then said his objective to list was to take the company to the public and not just limit the gains from it to a handful of investors. Dhirubhai believed that anyone in India, however humble their beginnings were, deserved a share in the country’s growth, as part-owners. “He (had) asked ordinary families to trust him. And they did, with their savings, and with their dreams. Almost 50 years later, that trust has come full circle,” she said.Jio has about 54 crore customers. Its hugely successful IPO was subscribed over 22 times, with nearly 1.3 crore investors wanting to have a pie in the company. India’s largest IPO was fully subscribed within barely 100 minutes of its launch, making it the fastest in the country’s history and prompting quips about “Jio’s 100m dash” — a play on the popular term for a 100-metre race.Compared to an indicative listing price of Rs 1,370 that was derived from the trend in the unofficial market, Jio listed slightly off that mark on Wednesday. However, late buying, believed to be mainly by foreign funds, took the stock price beyond Rs 1,400 and the company’s market cap beyond Rs 13 lakh crore, exchange data showed. The hugely successful IPO and the listing also took the RIL group to the top slot among the most valued business houses in India. At a combined market cap of Rs 30.3 lakh crore, it just raced past the incumbent Tata group, now at Rs 25.4 lakh crore, data from ETIntelligence showed.During the listing ceremony, Jio Platforms director Anant Ambani said he wanted to express gratitude to the millions who believed in Jio. He also paid rich tributes to his grandfather, Dhirubhai Ambani, and his father, Mukesh Ambani, “who dreamt big and believed Bharat should not be behind anyone”.Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said that in the next ten years, the company’s aim is “to democratise every technology that can transform Indian lives: AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity even from space, and digital services not yet imagined. Our ambition is a truly digital society, with Jio Platforms at its core: one where connectivity, computing and intelligence work seamlessly together, and every Indian, in every corner and every language, can participate, progress and prosper.”The stock was ceremonially listed on NSE after a bell-ringing ceremony. After the first quote at Rs 1,358, the stock touched a high of Rs 1,424 and a low of Rs 1,357. On listing day, between the two bourses, about 19.4 crore Jio shares were traded. One of the noteworthy aspects of the IPO was that none of the existing shareholders in the company that included promoter RIL and global tech giants like Google and Meta sold any shares in the offer.You use AI every day.
