articles.title: Ex-presidente do BRB pressionou por compras de carteiras do Master mesmo após alertas, diz PF | G1
articles.standfirst: Relatório aponta que Paulo Henrique Costa cobrava rapidez na análise e liquidação de operações, mesmo diante de inconsistências nas carteiras apresentadas pelo Banco Master.
articles.summary: Relatório aponta que Paulo Henrique Costa cobrava rapidez na análise e liquidação de operações mesmo diante de inconsistências nas carteiras apresentadas pelo Banco Master.
articles.body:
O ex-presidente do Banco de Brasília (BRB), Paulo Henrique Costa, pressionou áreas internas do banco para acelerar a análise e a conclusão de operações com o Banco Master – mesmo após receber alertas sobre problemas nas carteiras de crédito apresentadas pela instituição privada.

Mensagens analisadas pelos investigadores mostram que Paulo Henrique Costa cobrava rapidez, estabelecia prioridades e indicava quais operações deveriam ser concluídas.

Em dezembro de 2024, após a identificação de irregularidades em uma carteira que ainda estava sob análise, o presidente escreveu que era necessário olhar "esses 71 mm [R$ 71 milhões] rápido" .

Em resposta, o então diretor de Finanças do BRB, Dario Oswaldo Garcia Junior afirmou que iria pressionar a equipe responsável pela análise. "Tô aqui no Robério para apertar."

"Paulo Henrique definia as operações prioritárias, os respectivos montantes e os prazos de conclusão, além de cobrar pessoalmente sua execução pela Diretoria Financeira do BRB", diz o relatório.

Fachada de prédio do BRB, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Pressão por operações de mais de R$ 1 bilhão

Em outro diálogo, de 23 de dezembro, Paulo Henrique Costa enumerou cinco operações que pretendia concluir , em movimentações que somavam cerca de R$ 1 bilhão entre compras de carteiras e vendas de créditos inadimplentes.

“Nos organizamos para concluir os seguintes movimentos: 1. Compra de credcesta no limite que temos (R$ 408 mm). 2. Liquidação da venda de NPL pendente de pagamento (R$ 200 mm + atualização). 3.Compra de credcesta no limite adicional (R$ 196 mm). 4. Compra de credcesta (sênior) usando seguro prestamista (R$ 70 mm). 5. Venda de nova tranche de NPL, no valor de R$ 150 mm", indica o relatório da PF.

Segundo a investigação, o então presidente indicou como prioridade a liquidação, ainda naquele dia, de duas operações de R$ 408 milhões e R$ 200 milhões. Ele também indicou que o ideal seria concluir uma terceira, de R$ 196 milhões.

"O ideal é resolvermos os itens 1 e 2 hoje, e os itens 3, 4 e 5 na quinta.”; "Foco nessas cessões. Vc precisa de alguma ajuda nisso"; "O ideal seria já liquidar os R$ 408 + R$ 196 mm ainda hoje", disse Paulo Henrique Costa em mensagens.

De acordo com o documento, as operações eram organizadas não apenas para atender às demandas de liquidez do Banco Master, mas com um cronograma de aquisições.

"Assim, sua atuação não pode ser reduzida à supervisão institucional própria do cargo de Presidente. Paulo Henrique exercia comando direto sobre a execução das operações, mobilizava as áreas técnicas para atender aos prazos pretendidos, ajustava o cronograma às necessidades do Banco Master e utilizava os efeitos contábeis das cessões como justificativa para sua continuidade", destaca o documento da PF.

O BRB – que tem como acionista majoritário o governo do DF – enfrenta uma crise marcada por perdas bilionárias ligadas a operações com o extinto Banco Master.

Paulo Henrique Costa, Daniel Vorcaro e Augusto Lima foram alvo de diferentes fases da Operação Compliance Zero, que investiga os negócios do Banco Master. Costa e Vorcaro estão presos.

O BRB tentou comprar o Master e chegou a injetar R$ 16,7 bilhões no banco de Vorcaro. A compra foi barrada pelo Banco Central e, depois, o BRB descobriu que parte das carteiras compradas era fraudulenta e sem lastro.

Alertas sobre as carteiras já circulavam no BRB

De acordo com o relatório, Paulo Henrique recebeu alertas sobre margens consideradas incompatíveis, índices de inadimplência de 28% e 15% e falhas nas planilhas utilizadas nas operações.

A PF chama atenção para a responsabilidade da Diretoria Colegiada (DICOL) do BRB de barrar negociações com informações incompletas e inconformidade com as normas.

A investigação, no entanto, mostra que 13 das 14 notas executivas — documentos que iniciavam o processo de aquisição — foram aprovadas antes mesmo da conclusão dos pareceres técnicos .

Operações fracionadas para driblar conselho

Outra informação em destaque no relatório é o fracionamento das aquisições das carteiras .

A manobra ocorria porque a Diretoria Colegiada do BRB só podia deliberar sobre compra e venda de carteiras com valor máximo de R$ 750 milhões. Acima disso, era preciso acionar o Conselho de Administração do banco.

Segundo o relatório, o colegiado aprovou 25 transações, que totalizam R$ 17,5 bilhões. Dessas, 21 foram fixadas em exatos R$ 750 milhões, valor máximo para deliberação.

Somado, o montante corresponde a 23,3 vezes o limite de negociação da Diretoria Colegiada.

Veja abaixo quem são os 15 indiciados pela Polícia Federal no relatório desta quarta (28):

Daniel Vorcaro , ex-dono do Banco Master;

Paulo Henrique Costa , ex-presidente do BRB;

Augusto Lima , ex-sócio de Vorcaro no Banco Master;

Angelo Antônio Ribeiro da Silva , ex-diretor do Master;

Luiz Antônio Bull , ex-diretor do Master;

Alberto Félix de Oliveira Neto , ex-diretor do Master;

Allan da Silva Machado , ex-procurador do Master;

Henrique Souza e Silva Peretto , sócio da Tirreno;

André Felipe de Oliveira Seixas Maia , sócio da Tirreno;

Daniel Lopes Monteiro , ex-advogado do Master;

Dario Oswaldo Garcia Junior , ex-diretor de Finanças e Controladoria do BRB;

Luana de Andrade Ribeiro , ex-diretora executiva de Controle e Riscos do BRB;

Cristiane Maria Lima Bukowitz , ex-diretora executiva de gestão de pessoas do BRB;

Diogo Ilário de Araújo Oliveira , ex-diretor executivo de Atacado e Governo do BRB;

José Maria Correa Dias Junior , ex-diretor executivo de Tecnologia do BRB.

seis ex-sócios ou ex-gestores do Banco Master;

dois sócios da Tirreno, firma de consultoria apontada pela PF como empresa de fachada para o esquema;

O g1 e a TV Globo tentam contato com as defesas dos citados.

"A defesa de Daniel Vorcaro tomou conhecimento do relatório parcial apresentado pela Polícia Federal no Inquérito nº 5026/STF, que promove o indiciamento de Daniel. Trata-se de um ato açodado e afoito, que antecipa conclusões que a própria investigação admite ainda não ter alcançado:

● Indiciamento antes do fim da investigação: no mesmo documento em que indicia, a autoridade policial pede ao Supremo Tribunal Federal mais 60 dias para prosseguir nas apurações. Reconhece que exames periciais seguem “em elaboração”, que parte do material apreendido não foi analisada e que pessoas relevantes sequer foram ouvidas. Indicia-se primeiro para investigar depois.

● Inexistência de prejuízo ao BRB: o negócio envolvendo as carteiras da Tirreno não foi concluído. As carteiras foram substituídas por outros ativos, e a troca realizada demonstra que os negócios entre o Banco Master e o BRB geraram resultados positivos para o Banco de Brasília. Nenhuma perícia oficial apurou qualquer prejuízo: os números citados no relatório vêm da petição inicial de uma ação indenizatória movida pelo próprio BRB, que é parte interessada, e a própria Polícia Federal reconhece que não teve acesso ao resultado da auditoria sobre os ativos entregues em substituição. A defesa já pediu, na esfera cível, a perícia que sepultará definitivamente a narrativa fantasiosa de fraude e prejuízo.

● Lavagem de dinheiro sem rastreamento de recursos: o relatório imputa lavagem de capitais, mas registra que ainda está pendente a análise bancária, fiscal e patrimonial destinada a “identificar eventual proveito econômico” e “rastrear os fluxos financeiros”. Imputa-se a ocultação de valores cujo caminho sequer foi examinado.

● Indiciamento frágil e absurdo: as conclusões se apoiam em leitura seletiva de mensagens e em hipóteses formuladas “em tese”, e não em demonstração técnica. São operações embasadas em decisões técnicas e colegiadas das instâncias de governança de duas instituições supervisionadas pelo Banco Central. Agora são retratadas como crime sem que se tenha aferido seu resultado econômico.

● O depoimento que não vazou: Daniel Vorcaro prestou à Polícia Federal esclarecimentos decisivos sobre as operações com o BRB. Foi um depoimento esclarecedor e, curiosamente, justamente ele não foi vazado.

● Arquivamento do Inquérito e Revogação da Prisão: sem prova técnica de fraude ou de prejuízo, o indiciamento não se sustenta, e o inquérito relativo às operações entre o Banco Master e o BRB deve ser arquivado. Nesse contexto, torna-se urgente e imperativa a revogação da prisão preventiva de Daniel Vorcaro, garantindo-se seu direito de responder em liberdade. Brasília, 28 de outubro de 2026."

"A defesa de Paulo Henrique Costa, ex-Presidente do BRB, recebeu com surpresa o seu indiciamento pelos crimes de gestão fraudulenta e de organização criminosa. Pesa dizer que o trabalho policial submeteu os fatos às hipóteses acusatórias, quando deveria fazer o inverso.

As conversas em aplicativos de mensageria nos celulares dos integrantes do ambiente Master mostram às escâncaras que Paulo Henrique não tinha conhecimento das fraudes nas carteiras. As testemunhas, sejam as ligadas ao BRB, sejam ao Master, são convergentes nesse tema. Também foram ignorados todos os documentos carreados aos autos, inclusive por autoridades públicas, como o Banco Central.

Há prova eloquente de que foi Paulo Henrique a detectar irregularidades nas carteiras; de que ele exigiu, passo contínuo, 25 bilhões de garantias; de que quando o nome da Tirreno vem à lume, as operações são suspensas; há centenas e centenas de mensagens de Paulo Henrique ao Master exigindo a substituição de ativos, na forma dos contratos, inclusive se valendo daqueles dados em garantia. Foi Paulo Henrique quem trouxe o fato ao conhecimento do Banco Central, a quem se participaram todos os passos, antes e depois da detecção da fraude.

Curiosamente, não se aponta nenhuma vantagem financeira de Paulo Henrique; a fantasiosa versão de recepção de apartamentos, na ordem de 150 milhões de reais, foi amplamente descartada, embora tenham fundamentado a prisão preventiva a que ainda está submetido, já há mais de 180 dias, sem revisão judicial, em ofensa a previsão expressa do Código de Processo Penal. Há pedido de liberdade provisória desde 12 de junho, pendente de opinião da PGR; há habeas corpus impetrado há 20, sem sequer remessa ao MPF.

Paulo Henrique seguiu as orientações do acionista majoritário de realizar operação societária com o Master, seguiu toda a governança, dividiu todos os passos com o Conselho de Administração e com o Banco Central. Sempre atuou no melhor interesse do BRB. Todas as decisões, importante frisar, eram colegiadas; o Presidente do BRB tinha alçada de zero reais. Nenhuma decisão foi tomada por ele, sozinho.

As autoridades usam enviesado microscópio na carteira de 12,2 bi - dos quais 10,5 bi foram substituídos por ativos hígidos, até sua remoção do cargo - e esquecem que a relação com o Master gerou 8 bilhões de reais de receitas; e seguem gerando, diga-se.

Quando Paulo Henrique foi erradamente removido do BRB, o banco era saudável, líquido, rentável, com marca positiva e líder em diversos segmentos; sempre cumpriu seu relevante papel de banco público. Paulo Henrique sempre leal ao BRB e defendeu seu interesse; e seguiu fazendo na relação com o Master.

Paulo Henrique e sua defesa seguem acreditando na Justiça e que a Procuradoria-Geral da República saberá reconhecer a totalidade dos elementos contidos nos autos; uma leitura idônea levará o Ministério Público Federal a descartar as hipóteses de gestão fraudulenta e a igualmente estapafúrdia conclusão de que Paulo Henrique integraria uma organização criminosa."

A defesa de Augusto Lima rechaça integralmente a conclusão do relatório parcial. A documentação e os esclarecimentos apresentados por Augusto Lima demonstram, de forma veemente, que ele não participou, direta ou indiretamente, da fraude mencionada.

A conclusão equivocada da Autoridade Policial em relação a Augusto Lima decorre da leitura enviesada de esparsas e aleatórias mensagens de texto, temporalmente desconectadas entre si.

A defesa ressalta que se trata de conclusão apresentada em relatório parcial de investigação, que não constitui denúncia do Ministério Público nem condenação judicial. A presunção de inocência é uma garantia constitucional e deve ser respeitada, sem antecipação de culpa.

A defesa reforça que confia no Poder Judiciário e que demonstrará, mais uma vez, o erro de premissa adotado pela Autoridade Policial, o que, inequivocamente, levará à exclusão de Augusto Lima da investigação.

articles.title: Noel seeks greater scrutiny of investments by Tata Sons
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, the controlling shareholder of Tata Sons, has called for greater scrutiny of large investments by the holding
articles.body: MUMBAI: Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, the controlling shareholder of Tata Sons, has called for greater scrutiny of large investments by the holding company, requiring management to present detailed business cases setting out the rationale, expected financial returns and risks of capital commitments before directors sign off on them, said people familiar with the matter.The intervention stems from concerns raised by Noel during Tata Sons board discussions this fiscal year, when a composite investment proposal worth more than Rs 23,000 crore was brought before directors for approval. The composite investment proposal included capital infusions in Air India, Tejas Networks, Tata Digital and other Tata operating entities.At the June board meeting, Noel said that proposals involving substantial capital commitments needed a formal assessment of expected financial returns and risks rather than being presented solely for approval, the people said.He has leverage. Tata Sons' articles of association require investments above Rs 100 crore to secure the affirmative support of a majority of Trusts-nominated directors. Noel, who took over the Trusts after the death of his half-brother Ratan Tata in Oct 2024, is one of two such nominees. The other is Venu Srinivasan, chairman emeritus of TVS Motor Company.During the Tata Sons board meeting in Sept, Noel repeated his demand that future investment proposals be accompanied by detailed business cases, the people said. That meeting considered no pending or fresh investment proposals and instead focused on the reappointment of Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran for another five-year term and the company's response to RBI directives.Noel and other directors had already clashed at that meeting over governance matters and Chandrasekaran's extension. Noel has since challenged the validity of the board's decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran, arguing the resolution was not on the meeting agenda and was therefore procedurally flawed.The disputes come amid a wider debate over Tata Sons' future. RBI rejected the company's application to surrender its registration as a core investment company (CIC). Since then, Noel has proposed merging two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company as part of efforts to avoid a public listing, while Reserve Bank governor Sanjay Malhotra has reiterated that CICs classified in the regulator's upper layer are mandated to list.You use AI every day. articles.title: EPFO looks to invest in startups, AIFs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Five years after govt allowed the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to invest in alternate investment funds (AIFs), the retirement
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five years after govt allowed the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to invest in alternate investment funds (AIFs), the retirement savings body is now working to come up with guidelines to enable its investments in these high-growth asset classes and startups.A proposal to allocate up to 3% of its fresh annual accretions into category I and category II AIFs regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) was discussed in the investment committee (IC) meeting last Thursday, TOI has learnt. In Sept, department for promotion of industry and internal trade (DPIIT) wrote to EPFO seeking participation in the recently-launched Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0.That provided the context to examine the broader approach towards AIF investments, persons privy to the discussions told TOI.Initially, the plan is to channel worker capital through institutional giants such as National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Sidbi’s Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0. The proposal will now be discussed by the central board of trustees (CBT), led by labour minister Mansukh Mandaviya in Nov.This move marks a shift from traditional, ultra-safe debt instruments towards risk capital, aiming to potentially generate higher long-term returns for crores of its salaried subscribers. According to the pattern of investment notified by the finance ministry, EPFO can invest up to 5% of its fresh accretions in asset-backed and trust-structured investments. It is yet to make any investments in category I and category II AIFs regulated by Sebi. EPFO currently manages around Rs 30 lakh crore belonging to nearly 30 crore members.Category I AIFs are development-oriented funds that support sectors with positive economic spillovers, such as startups, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), infrastructure, social ventures, and venture capital, while Category II AIFs include private equity (PE) funds, real estate funds, and private debt funds that do not fit into Category I or III and do not use leverage or borrowing.To protect workers’ funds against market volatility, the proposal embeds strict risk safeguards such as a mandatory minimum AIF corpus of Rs 100 crore, single-fund exposure caps, strict prohibitions against foreign-incorporated investments, and a requirement that fund managers remain independent of promoters.You use AI every day. articles.title: HUL sees strongest sales growth in 14 quarters, net up 4%
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Consumer goods major Hindustan Unilever on Wednesday reported a 3.8% increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 2,796 crore in the Sept quarter,
articles.body: BENGALURU: Consumer goods major Hindustan Unilever on Wednesday reported a 3.8% increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 2,796 crore in the Sept quarter, while revenue rose 14.4% to Rs 18,386 crore, indicating strong growth despite cost pressure.Underlying sales growth stood at 15%, the highest in 14 quarters, while volume growth accelerated to 7% from 5% in the June quarter. HUL also recorded price growth of about 8% during the Sept quarter.“We see both urban and rural growth at this moment,” MD & CEO Priya Nair said. HUL said its rural business had improved sequentially over the past four quarters but did not disclose separate rural and urban growth rates.The company is keeping a close tab on costs. “We took calibrated price increases only to cover the absolute impact of the higher cost,” CFO Niranjan Gupta said during an analyst call. HUL will consider further increases depending on how input costs move. It expects commodity inflation to remain elevated in the near term, although management said the June and September quarters had borne much of the recent increase.Nair said the company will look to shore up volumes to help deliver revenue and profit.Home care led the quarter, with underlying sales rising 22% on double-digit volume growth. However, its segment profit grew only 2.6% to Rs 1,111 crore, while revenue rose 21.4% to Rs 6,878 crore. The segment’s margin fell to 16.2% from 19.1%.“When input costs go up steeply in a category like home care, there’s always a lag in price versus cost,” Nair said. articles.title: TVS Motor Company to demerge consumer finance business
articles.summary: CHENNAI: TVS Motor Company, a leading two and three-wheeler maker, will demerge its consumer-finance-related investments into a separate listed holding
articles.body: CHENNAI: TVS Motor Company, a leading two and three-wheeler maker, will demerge its consumer-finance-related investments into a separate listed holding company, marking a significant shift in the TVS Venu group’s strategy, as a financial services business built over 15 years of investment emerges as an independent growth engine alongside its core mobility business.The proposed demerger, approved by the board on Wednesday, will transfer TVS Motor’s investment in TVS Credit Services and certain other non-core investments to the new entity. Existing TVS Motor shareholders, including promoters and public investors, will receive an equal number of shares in the new entity, in proportion to their current holdings. TVS Motor will not retain a direct stake in the new company.“India’s rapidly expanding financial services sector offers tremendous opportunities for long-term growth,” said Sudarshan Venu, chairman of TVS Motor Company. The new structure would give the businesses greater strategic autonomy to pursue opportunities and deploy capital according to their growth priorities, while enabling shareholders to continue participating in the future growth of both businesses, he added.The group is already consolidating its NBFC operations in line with an RBI directive. articles.title: Adani explores buyout of Dutch energy co VTTI
articles.summary: Billionaire Gautam Adani, India’s richest person, is exploring a potential acquisition of Dutch energy storage group VTTI as supply disruptions make the
articles.body: Billionaire Gautam Adani, India’s richest person, is exploring a potential acquisition of Dutch energy storage group VTTI as supply disruptions make the facilities more valuable for energy trading, people familiar with the matter said.Adani Group, the tycoon’s power-to-ports conglomerate, is among suitors that have been evaluating Rotterdam-based VTTI, according to the people. A deal could value the company at around $3.4 billion, they said.Australian infrastructure manager IFM Investors Pty and energy and commodities group Vitol SA each own around 45% of VTTI, while Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. holds the remaining 10%. Adnoc is considering selling out of VTTI completely and the other co-owners may also look to reduce their positions in the company in any deal, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing confidential information.Deliberations are ongoing and there’s no certainty they’ll result in a transaction, the people said. Other bidders have also been pursuing a stake in VTTI, they said. A representative for Adani Group didn’t immediately respond to queries. Spokespeople for IFM, Adnoc and VTTI declined to comment. A representative for Vitol didn’t immediately comment.VTTI operates terminals used to store fuels and chemicals, including fossil fuels, biofuels and solvents. The company has a global presence. Adani Group’s portfolio houses infrastructure assets including airports, roads and data centers, as well as mining and defense assets. Its founder is India’s wealthiest person with an estimated net worth of about $105.7 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.Listed flagship Adani Enterprises in July raised Rs 15,000 crore ($1.6 billion) from institutional investors to help fund capital expenditures and possible debt repayment. The following month, Gautam Adani won dismissal of US securities fraud charges — a victory in a blockbuster case that had threatened his conglomerate’s expansion. Adani Group has been looking at acquisitions overseas to help accelerate growth. articles.title: 3 Wall Street firms agree to pay up to $100,000 a month to get Trump’s posts faster: How it works
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump’s paid social media service, Truth API, has found customers, with Bloomberg and two high-frequency trading firms paying for
articles.body: US President Donald Trump’s paid social media service, Truth API, has found customers, with Bloomberg and two high-frequency trading firms paying for faster access to his posts. The service costs financial institutions up to $100,000 a month.Two sources with direct knowledge of the matter, cited by Reuters, said Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading, both of which specialise in algorithmic and automated trading strategies, have also signed up for the service.The deals give subscribers a timing advantage over people who monitor Trump’s posts on the app themselves.The arrangement has raised concerns about the sale of faster access to statements by a sitting president, particularly because his posts can influence financial markets.It also comes as Trump Media and Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social, faces legal challenges over the paid service and questions about the potential use of presidential communications for commercial gain.How Truth API worksTrump Media and Technology Group announced the faster-access product in July, pitching it to trading firms and other financial institutions. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social.Trump Media officials have put the timing advantage at 50 milliseconds. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.High-frequency traders rely on software to scan news headlines, company announcements and government statements for information that could move markets. Their systems can read and analyse the information before executing trades in thousandths of a second.The potential consequences of Trump’s social media posts were evident in April, when oil futures fell after he announced a ceasefire in the Iran war on Truth Social.An application programming interface, or API, acts as a digital bridge that allows one computer system to communicate with another. In this case, the product gives subscribers faster access to the president’s posts, which they can use in their trading or financial information systems.Who is paying for the service?According to a Reuters report, Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API.In August, Trump Media told investors it had "signed more than 10 customer agreements”. Reuters was unable to independently confirm that figure.The company did not identify its customers but said they were primarily Wall Street trading firms paying between $60,000 and $100,000 a month. The latest deals indicate that the product has attracted both financial trading firms and a news and data provider.Reuters, which competes with Bloomberg in financial news, said in a statement: "We will assess the service, but have no current plans to subscribe."Trump Media defended the product in a statement, saying: “Truth Social offers an industry-standard API product for which there is significant demand across industries. We take customer confidentiality seriously. This reporting is based on misleading information being peddled by anonymous sources aimed at harming our company, customers and shareholders.”The company has not publicly named the subscribers in its August investor update, and the three firms named in the report declined to comment.Why the paid feed has drawn criticismThe paid service has drawn criticism for giving subscribers faster access to a president’s statements, potentially offering financial firms an advantage when his posts move markets. The deals are likely the first time a business linked to a sitting president has sold access to his statements.In July, Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Adam Schiff of California asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether the service violated securities laws. They called it a “shocking abuse” of office by a president seeking personal gain.A Trump Media and Technology Group spokesperson said, “Congressional Democrats continue to mischaracterize Truth API either out of ideological opposition to free markets or a failure to grasp the distinction between public and nonpublic information.”In August, Intercept Media and the non-profit Freedom of the Press Foundation sued Trump, seeking to stop the White House from posting official government announcements exclusively on Truth Social. The ongoing lawsuit describes the service as "profoundly corrupt" and alleges violations of the First and Fifth Amendments.Trump Media’s financial portfolioThe commercial arrangement has also drawn attention to the ownership of Trump Media. The president’s family trust owns 41% of the company, and Trump is the trust’s sole beneficiary.The Truth API deals come as Trump Media faces a steep decline in its stock market value.Shares of the company have fallen more than 50% so far this year. Its market value has also been volatile since it went public in March 2024.The company closed at a market value of about $8 billion on its debut in March 2024, but is now worth about $1.8 billion.Since 2024, Trump Media has lost about $1.76 billion, including non-cash charges.You use AI every day. articles.title: Industrial output grows 6.7% on manufacturing, electricity
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Industrial production grew 6.7% in Sept as against 6.1% expansion recorded a year ago, on account of strong manufacturing and electricity
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Industrial production grew 6.7% in Sept as against 6.1% expansion recorded a year ago, on account of strong manufacturing and electricity output.Sequentially, however, industrial production witnessed deceleration from a downward revised figure of 7.8% in Aug, official data released Wednesday showed. During April-Sept, the index of industrial production (IIP) grew 6.8%, compared with 4.4% a year ago.Manufacturing, which has a weight of 76% in the index, grew 7.6% as 17 out of 23 industry groups witnessed an increase in output, led by beverages, electrical equipment, transport equipment, rubber, textiles, furniture among others.Electricity and gas supply expanded 11.2% on account of higher temperature due to heat wave conditions. Electricity production from conventional sources recorded double-digit growth (16.5%) in Sept, while there was a moderate growth in electricity output from renewable sources (4.3%). The newly added water supply, sewerage and waste management sector grew 5.8%. Activity in the mining and quarrying contracted further (-6.2%) during the month, led by the non-metallic minerals segment with output declining in eight of the last nine months.In the use-based category -- capital goods (10.4%) and intermediate goods (12.2%) industries registered double-digit output, reflecting the impact of sustained public capex in the economy. Capital goods, too, grew 7.2% during the month.Output in consumer durables, which reflect consumer sentiments, witnessed deceleration (6%) during the month, while consumer non-durables recorded acceleration in growth (1.4%) in Sept, after remaining in the contractionary zone in Aug.You use AI every day. articles.title: Oil prices slip as peace hopes ease supply fears, Middle East tensions limit losses
articles.summary: Oil prices declined on Thursday as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic developments between the US and Iran against the risk of further
articles.body: Oil prices declined on Thursday as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic developments between the US and Iran against the risk of further supply disruptions from escalating attacks in the Middle East.Brent crude fell by $0.85, or 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%, to $101.90. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%.The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to restart peace negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.The possibility of further negotiations has offered some relief to oil markets, but the threat of an intensification in regional hostilities continues to weigh on the outlook for supplies. Concerns include renewed attacks by Yemen's Houthis and the possibility that the US could launch an attack on Iran after its mid-term elections on November 3.Houthi attacks keep supply concerns aliveFresh developments in the conflict involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia added to uncertainty on Thursday. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's eastern region early in the day, with hostilities between the two sides showing no signs of easing.The latest incident followed an attack on Aden airport on Wednesday, according to Yemeni government forces. A day earlier, the Houthis had said they struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery with a missile, escalating their attacks against the world's second-largest crude producer after the United States.Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the reported strike on the refinery, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day.The continuing attacks have kept concerns over potential supply disruptions in focus even as diplomatic efforts offer the possibility of easing tensions.Conflicting signals from US-Iran peace effortsEfforts to find a way to end the war involving the US, Israel and Iran have produced mixed signals. An official briefed on the negotiations said Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft agreement to end the conflict.However, a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals, describing them as unacceptable ideas that did not constitute an offer.Iran's foreign minister said on Wednesday that Tehran was continuing to give diplomacy a chance to succeed. The minister also flagged the possibility of completing Iran's seven-day plan in less than a week if it was adopted.The contrasting positions leave the prospects for a diplomatic resolution uncertain, while the possibility of renewed negotiations has contributed to the downward movement in crude prices.Meanwhile, US inventory data provided another factor for oil markets to follow. The US Energy Information Administration said that energy companies had withdrawn 1.9 million barrels of crude oil from storage during the week ended October 23.Gasoline inventories, however, increased by 3.9 million barrels, against analysts' expectations of a decline of 900,000 barrels.The opposing movements in crude and gasoline stockpiles added to the mixed signals facing oil markets as traders assessed the impact of diplomatic developments, regional attacks and US inventory data on prices.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kalshi, cofounders hit with criminal charges in US state of Utah
articles.summary: The charges come after a federal judge ruled that Utah could enforce its anti-gambling laws against prediction markets.
articles.body:
The US state of Utah has announced criminal charges against popular prediction market Kalshi and its two cofounders, accusing the platform and its executives of illegally promoting online gambling.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed the charges against Kalshi, chief executive officer Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara on Wednesday, a day after US President Donald Trump’s administration sued the state to block its civil enforcement actions against the platform.

According to the criminal complaint filed in a Salt Lake City court, Kalshi facilitated an undercover law enforcement officer’s wagers on sports events, including games in the NFL.

The charges come after a federal judge in August ruled that Utah was entitled to enforce its stringent anti-gambling laws against online prediction markets, following a legal bid by Kalshi to block enforcement of the law.

The criminal complaint accuses the defendants of 12 counts of online gambling promotion, one count of general gambling promotion and one count of pattern of unlawful activity.

Kalshi and Brown’s office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Utah has some of the strictest prohibitions against gambling in the US, with its state constitution explicitly barring lawmakers from legalising the activity.

The charges mark an escalation in a showdown between US states and the Trump administration over the regulation of prediction markets.

On Tuesday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed a lawsuit seeking to block Utah’s enforcement actions against prediction markets, arguing that the platforms fall under federal jurisdiction.

The regulator announced the move after Utah last week filed a civil lawsuit accusing Kalshi of facilitating betting on sports, elections, politics and other outcomes in violation of anti-gambling laws.

Dozens of US states, led by both Republican and Democratic administrations, have argued that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission does not have the authority to regulate prediction markets.

Last month, the state of New Jersey asked the US Supreme Court to rule on whether state or federal authorities have jurisdiction over sports betting on prediction market platforms.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Planning a quick trip to the bank today? You might want to check the holiday calendar first.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Planning a quick trip to the bank today? You might want to check the holiday calendar first.The festive season brings a fresh round of bank holidays, but closures are not the same across India, as they depend on the festivals and regional occasions observed in each state.Today, October 29, banks in Himachal Pradesh are closed for Karwa Chauth. But if you are elsewhere in the country, the holiday schedule may be different. Therefore, a quick check before stepping out for your bank related errands could save you an unnecessary trip to the branch.Upcoming holidaysAfter the Karwa Chauth holiday in Himachal Pradesh on October 29, Gujarat is set to see bank closures on October 31 to mark Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.Bank customers will also need to keep track of the holidays scheduled for November, when several festivals and regional observances are expected to affect branch operations in different states. articles.title: Rupee gains 11 paise to 95.17 against dollar after Fed holds interest rates
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rupee strengthened against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, rising 11 paise to 95.17 after the American currency softened following
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rupee strengthened against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, rising 11 paise to 95.17 after the American currency softened following the US Federal Reserve's latest policy decision. The currency opened at 95.20 at the interbank foreign exchange market before moving higher. It had settled at 95.28 against the dollar in the previous session.The US central bank kept its interest rates unchanged in the 3.75 per cent–4.00 per cent range, as expected. Despite the widely anticipated decision, the market response was mildly negative for the dollar, forex traders said.The rupee continues to face pressure from elevated crude oil prices and firm US yields. However, foreign exchange reserves of around $721 billion, a recent improvement in portfolio flows and the Reserve Bank of India's presence in the market are providing support to the currency."We therefore see a gradual upward bias in USD-INR within the range, rather than evidence of a disorderly move," Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research, Kotak NEO told PTI.Markets are now closely watching incoming economic data following the Fed's decision to hold rates steady. Stronger inflation figures could reinforce expectations of a rate hike in December, whereas softer numbers could offer relief to bullion and emerging-market currencies.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, slipped 0.04 per cent to 102.15. Brent crude futures, meanwhile, fell 1.03 per cent to $114.13 per barrel.Domestic equities also traded higher in early deals on Thursday. BSE Sensex advanced over 550 points to 73,409.06, while NSE Nifty50 climbed above the 22,730 points. articles.title: Anthropic's IPO filing left these key questions unanswered
articles.summary: Anthropic's hotly anticipated S-1 filing finally dropped this week, providing investors with greater visibility into its financials, ownership structure, and...
articles.body:
Anthropic's hotly anticipated S-1 filing finally dropped Monday, providing investors with greater visibility into its financials, ownership structure, and potential risks .

But there are plenty of questions the document didn't answer that will be vital in helping investors decide whether to buy the stock. Some clarity could come before the IPO. Other lingering uncertainties might not be resolved for years.

First, creating short-term suspense, the prospectus contained several prominent omissions that will likely be included in an amended filing before the IPO. They include third quarter financials and details on share-lockup expirations — when insiders are allowed to sell. The expiration schedule currently includes dates but not the number of shares affected.

The most important interim question is where Anthropic shares will be priced. It's tough to decide whether to buy something if you don't know what it costs. Analysts can't get a handle on the public stock's valuation before pricing is announced.

Anthropic publicly files IPO prospectus, noting strong revenue growth and massive spending

When is the Anthropic IPO? The stock could start trading as soon as Nov. 16.

5 unexpected risk factors Anthropic is worried about

They won't have long to wait: A pricing range will be included in an amended filing that will be released when Anthropic begins its IPO roadshow . The debut is reportedly set for before the end of November, so investors will know firm pricing within weeks.

For the answers to other questions, investors will have to be more patient.

Companies typically don't put financial forecasts into an S-1. They're technically allowed, but businesses can be held liable for misstatements in a prospectus, so they tend to avoid them.

That's what Gil Luria, D.A. Davidson director of technology research, is waiting for. "Now I mostly want to know what guidance looks like for Q4 and 2027 — top and bottom line," he wrote in an email.

Anthropic's filing revealed more than $500 billion in compute spending commitments in the coming years. The cadence of that spend, however, is unclear, Cory Johnson of Epistrophy Capital said.

As he pointed out, a data center purchase is recognized once it's completed and turned over to the buyer, although there may be up-front payments as well. For Anthropic, "I want to know when those moments are, when those payments have to be made," Johnson said.

The answer to that question leads to another, larger one: "What does normalized profitability look like once the current infrastructure build-out matures?" Robert Schiffman, senior technology credit analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, asked.

"Revenue is scaling extraordinarily quickly, but with hundreds of billions of dollars of compute commitments, investors still don't have a clear picture of sustainable margins, returns on invested capital or how much revenue ultimately needs to be generated from each dollar of compute," Schiffman said.

articles.title: The strange math that shows how Trump got Venezuela to ‘gift’ oil to the United States
articles.summary: President Donald Trump made an extraordinary announcement this week: Venezuela had gifted the United States 1 million barrels of oil – and it didn’t cost American taxpayers a dime.
articles.body: President Donald Trump made an extraordinary announcement this week: Venezuela had gifted the United States 1 million barrels of oil – and it didn’t cost American taxpayers a dime. Tuesday’s announcement apparently surprised one important party to the deal: the producer of the Venezuelan oil. North American Blue Energy Partners, the US government’s partner in a major Venezuelan oil investment, initially announced Tuesday that the United States had purchased the 1 million barrels of oil, albeit at a substantially reduced price. After Trump said the oil was free, NABEP changed its statement to echo the president: The oil would arrive at a Texas port at no cost to the US taxpayer. The statements were both technically accurate: Venezuela is giving the United States a big gift of oil. The gift is even bigger than the 1 million barrels of “free” oil. What Trump said Trump made the oil-gift announcement on the way to a political rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, where he would show off oil tankers arriving at port with the first proceeds of NABEP’s partnership in Venezuela. “We took over Venezuela very successfully, and they’ve sent me as a gift a boatload of a million barrels of oil, and I’m giving that to the United States of America,” Trump told reporters. It wasn’t a figure of speech. The oil would be free for US taxpayers, Trump later wrote in a Truth Social post. “Thanks to our renewed relationship with Venezuela, which has turned out to be a truly excellent one, the Oil is being provided to the United States at NO cost to the American Taxpayer,” Trump wrote. At a rally on Tuesday evening, Trump said the United States’ January military operation in Venezuela that ousted President Nicolás Maduro represented “the greatest oil victory in history.” “See that little ship out there? It’s got 1 million barrels of oil on it from Venezuela, and we’re celebrating,” Trump said. “To the victor belong the spoils, right?” How the math works In an August agreement that the White House called the “biggest oil deal in world history,” the Pentagon took an equity stake in the company that owns NABEP, the second-largest private oil producer in Venezuela. NABEP’s owner is controlled by the family of Alejandro Betancourt López, a controversial international businessman based in the United Kingdom. As part of the deal, the US State Department has the right to purchase the first 20% of the Venezuelan oil produced by NABEP at $30 a barrel – the cost of production. That’s significantly lower than the price it could fetch on the open market. NABEP announced Tuesday that the first proceeds of its joint venture with the US government would arrive on two tankers in Corpus Christi. “The cargo is part of the U.S. government’s right to purchase 20% of NABEP’s production at cost, with no markup, a provision of the company’s August agreement with the U.S. Departments of State and War,” NABEP said in a statement. Later that day, NABEP updated its statement. “To recognize the historic nature of the agreement between NABEP and its new anchor buyer, the United States government, NABEP delivered the first million barrels of oil at no cost to the U.S. taxpayer,” the company added in its amended press release. How is that possible? NABEP agreed to deliver the 1 million barrels of oil for no up-front cost. It would make up for it by charging the government more for the oil in subsequent deliveries. “The cargo is being delivered pursuant to a commercial arrangement under which its value is settled through adjustments to future offtake pricing, rather than an upfront cash payment,” a person familiar with the deal’s terms said. In other words, the first million barrels were sold to the United States for $0 a barrel. The company will recoup those costs via deferred payments. For example, the next million barrels could be sold to the United States for $60 a barrel. Those shipments would even out to $30 a barrel. A spokesperson for the White House acknowledged that only the first shipment from NABEP would come at no cost to the US taxpayer. So everyone was truthful: The oil delivered to the United States this week was technically provided at no cost to the US taxpayer. And it was part of a previously arranged (and, on Tuesday, slightly amended) purchase agreement with NABEP. The actual ‘gift’ Even at $60 a barrel, the oil technically will arrive at no cost to the taxpayer. That’s because Venezuelan oil is selling for $80. So Venezuela will be sending the United States oil at a greatly reduced price from what it could fetch on the open market. The Trump administration argues that without foreign investment, the country could not take advantage of its oil riches. And the deal, regardless of the price of oil, will support Venezuelan jobs. That may be true. Venezuela’s socialist regimes left its oil infrastructure to decay over the past several decades, reducing its capacity to produce oil to around 1.2 million barrels per day, down from more than 3 million barrels in the 1990s. But the US extracting oil for cheap and selling it for a large profit is at best a bad look and at worst exploitative, critics say. “President Trump has purposefully covered up the details of his Venezuela oil scheme,” Illinois Democratic Rep. Dan Casten, a fierce critic of the administration’s Venezuela policy, told CNN. “We still don’t know exactly how much money is involved or where that money is going.” But Trump has always said Venezuela’s oil was for America’s taking. On January 3, when announcing the capture of Maduro, Trump said the military operation was about securing Venezuela’s resources, which are key to making America rich. “The future will be determined by the ability to protect commerce and territory and resources that are core to national security,” Trump said. “These are core to our national security. Just like tariffs are, they’ve made our country rich and they’ve made our national security strong, stronger than ever before. But these are the iron laws that have always determined global power. And we’re going to keep it that way.”

articles.title: The rest of Chipotle's year hinges on brisket
articles.summary: Chipotle has a lot riding on the launch of brisket in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
Chipotle ( CMG ) shares popped nearly 7% in pre-market trading on Thursday on hopes that a weak year will be wiped away by a strong fourth quarter, in large part because of the debut of brisket.

The company will bring back its fan favorite "mesquite smoked" brisket on Nov. 5.

"We continue to see reasons for improving same-store sales growth… Following earnings and our conversations with the company, we are maintaining our 4Q same-store sales growth estimate of 2% (consensus 2.9%) and believe brisket and additional marketing can support 3%–4% trends in November/December," EvercoreISI David Palmer said.

Palmer isn't alone on the Street in salivating at the potential of brisket for Chipotle to cap the year.

"Improving trends late in October, coupled with the launch of fan-favorite brisket and incremental marketing actions, give us confidence that comps can reach the 3%-4% range in November and December, paving the way for a stronger traffic start to 2027," said Bernstein analyst Danilo Gargiulo.

An argument could be made that Chipotle didn't earn the market reaction today, and an expected brisket sales bump shouldn't be priced in.

The company reported revenue of $3.29 billion, slightly topping Wall Street consensus estimates of roughly $3.28 billion.

But, the bottom line missed expectations as adjusted earnings landed at $0.27 per share, falling short of analyst projections of $0.29 per share due to rising labor and corporate overhead.

And same-store sales growth wasn't exactly sizzling at 2.1%.

"We continue to believe there is enough operational & marketing self-help to allow for traffic improvement and return to margin stability, while the stock's multiple has fully re-rated to reflect a more moderate – yet still well above average – growth profile," JP Morgan analyst John Ivankoe said.

For Chipotle's sake, the brisket better be so good people come back for it in December after trying it in November.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: In one of the biggest deals in Indian airport-hospitality space, Tata Group's Taj Hotels and Adani Airports have entered into an agreement for eight hotels across four cities -- Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati. Adani operates the airports in these cities and Taj Group will create a combined inventory of 2,000 rooms in the eight hotels that will span Indian Hotels Co Ltd (IHCL, Taj parent) brands across its luxury to mid scale brands -- Taj, Vivanta, Gateway and Ginger. This is part of Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL), India’s largest private airport operator, plans of developing integrated airport ecosystems that bring together aviation, hospitality, retail, commercial and lifestyle infrastructure.With this pact, AAHL has now partnered with leading hotel brands for 15 hotels across its key airports in India. The latest agreement encompasses three Taj hotels, two Vivanta hotels, one Gateway hotel and two Ginger hotels, providing hospitality offerings across multiple traveller segments.In Mumbai, the portfolio will include a Taj hotel at Terminal 2 - Mumbai airport. In Lucknow, the development will comprise a Vivanta and a Ginger hotel. Ahmedabad will include a Taj and a Vivanta in advance stages of development, while Guwahati will feature a Taj, Gateway and Ginger. The partnership envisages development of hotels by Adani Airports, which will be operated by IHCL.AAHL director Jeet Adani said: "Across the world, leading airports are evolving into integrated destinations that serve as catalysts for commerce, tourism and urban growth Our partnership with IHCL is an important step in this journey, bringing together our hospitality-led mixed-use destinations and India’s leading hospitality company to create world-class hotels across key airport cities with its brands including the iconic Taj. Together, we aim to strengthen the hospitality ecosystem within our Airport City developments and contribute to the long-term economic growth of the regions we serve.”IHCL MD and CEO Puneet Chhatwal said: “As India strengthens its position as one of the world’s fastest-growing aviation markets, airport-centric developments are emerging as important commercial and hospitality hubs. Our partnership with Adani Airport Holdings Limited brings together two leading Indian companies with a shared vision to build India’s travel and tourism sector.”Adani Airports has formed Adani Airport City Ltd to develop a land bank of over 655 acres across eight airports in seven states, including nearly 440 acres in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai. articles.title: European Central Bank President Lagarde resigns after months of speculation
articles.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced her resignation on Thursday, ending months of speculation about her future at a complex juncture for Europe and the ECB.
articles.body: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced her resignation on Thursday, ending months of speculation about her future at a complex juncture for Europe and the ECB. Lagarde will step down on February 7, giving current European Union leaders time to pick a successor well before a French presidential election that polls show far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is favorite to win. “European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde today informed the Governing Council and the President of the European Council António Costa that she will step down from her position on 7 February 2027,” the ECB said in a press release. The former central bank governors of the Netherlands and Spain, Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos, are seen as frontrunners to replace Lagarde. Lagarde’s term was scheduled to run until the end of October 2027 but speculation about an early departure had been mounting for months, with the World Economic Forum seen as a likely destination. The move comes as the ECB is in the middle of a rate-hiking cycle, seeking to prevent an oil-price shock linked to the Iran war from feeding into other prices and wages. But it must also contend with a surge in government bond yields — especially in debt-laden France — that has pushed up borrowing costs for households and businesses and which Lagarde has said will curb growth and inflation. Caught between persistent inflation fueled by a renewed surge in energy costs and deteriorating financing conditions, the ECB is widely expected to keep its deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday while signaling that another increase, potentially as soon as December, remains likely. The ECB is due to announce its interest rate decision at 1315 GMT on Thursday, followed by Lagarde’s regular press conference at 1345 GMT.

articles.title: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart for $17 billion
articles.summary: The acquisition looks to give DoorDash a bigger presence in online grocery delivery via Instacart’s established grocery marketplace.
articles.body: DoorDash has announced that it’s buying Instacart in a deal valued at approximately $17 billion. The acquisition will give DoorDash a bigger presence in online grocery delivery thanks to Instacart’s established grocery marketplace and retailer partnerships, with Instacart CEO Chris Rogers saying the deal will make “online grocery more seamless and affordable” for millions of households. DoorDash says the acquisition will give Instacart users acces to more than 50,000 additional stores, and allow DashPass and Instacart Plus members to “pay one membership fee instead of two.” The deal is expected to close “in the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028,” subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. When finalized, DoorDash says it will preserve Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app, so the services will remain separate instead of being merged into a single platform. In its post-close commitments, DoorDash said local grocers won’t be limited by platform exclusivity, and will be free to work with either delivery service. Instacart shoppers will also retain flexibility around their working hours and which orders to accept, and will be able to choose whether to take on DoorDash orders or just stick with shopping for Instacart. DoorDash, which started as a restaurant courier service, already has its own grocery delivery business, but that faces ongoing competition from Instacart, Uber, Walmart, and Amazon. DoorDash is also incentivized to diversify further because its rivals have been stepping into the food delivery territory it’s best known for, with Uber acquiring Postmates and Delivery Hero. Here’s what DoorDash said regarding increasing competition: > “Most grocery shopping still happens in stores, but more people are buying groceries and everyday goods online. They expect fast, affordable delivery and an easy way to order. The biggest online retailers and grocers are racing ahead, building their own delivery fleets, warehouses, membership programs, and AI shopping assistants. A grocer or retailer running on thin margins cannot build all of that alone, and with AI, the playing field risks being tilted even further away from local commerce.” Rumors around the deal started circulating last week after The Information reported that Instacart was in talks with rival platforms Uber and DoorDash regarding a potential sale. By Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported that DoorDash was in “advanced talks” with Instacart, and that a deal could be reached “as soon as this week.” That proved to be accurate, though finalization will take much longer — giving stockholders and regulators time to voice their feelings about the acquisition. “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the announcement. “Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery.”

articles.title: Lumentum stock jumps on report of possible merger with Marvell
articles.summary: Marvell stock declined on a report that the chip designer is in advanced talks to purchase optical parts maker Lumentum.
articles.body:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) stock dropped 11% on Thursday on reports that the AI chipmaker is in advanced talks to purchase optical parts maker Lumentum ( LITE ). Shares of Lumentum surged 5%.

What's behind the move: The potential multibillion-dollar mega deal between the semiconductor designer and Lumentum was first reported by Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter.

An agreement could be announced as soon as next week. Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, compared with Marvell's roughly $221 billion.

What else you need to know: The acquisition would give Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections.

Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company.

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 190% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied 140%.

articles.title: Last snapshot of the US economy before midterms shows stronger growth but higher inflation
articles.summary: US economic growth accelerated last quarter at its fastest pace in over a year; however, rising gas prices helped to lift inflation in September to a four-month high, new data showed Thursday.
articles.body: US economic growth accelerated last quarter at its fastest pace in over a year; however, rising gas prices helped to lift inflation in September to a four-month high, new data showed Thursday. The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose 0.5% from August, bringing the annual rate of inflation to 3.6% from 3.4%, according to new Commerce Department data, well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% inflation target. Economists were expecting the PCE price index to increase 0.5% from the prior month, with the annual rate rising to 3.6%, according to FactSet estimates. Excluding food and gas, categories that tend to be volatile, the core PCE price index rose 0.3% from August, lifting the annual rate to 3.1% from 3%. The PCE price index is part of the Commerce Department’s monthly Personal Income and Outlays report, which includes comprehensive data on how Americans earn, spend and save. Americans pumped the brakes on their spending last month, the report also showed. Consumer spending rose 0.5%, slowing from a gain of 0.9% the month before. When adjusting for inflation, consumer spending was flat from the month before. Consumer spending has held up despite broader economic shocks – including a war-driven spike in energy costs – but it has come partly at the expense of savings as income growth has slowed. Thursday’s report showed that the personal savings rate (savings as a percentage of after-tax income) fell 0.2 percentage points to 3.8%, the lowest rate in nearly four years. Personal income grew 0.2% from August, slowing from a rate of 0.3%. Separately on Thursday, the Commerce Department reported that US economic growth accelerated during the third quarter, with gross domestic product expanding at a 3.4% inflation-adjusted annualized rate, a faster pace than the 3.0% rate economists had projected. GDP captures the value of all goods and services across the economy. The latest reports land a day after Fed policymakers left interest rates unchanged, indicating a desire to consider more economic data before making their next policy move. Last month, the central bank raised rates for the first time in three years. But the rate increase has yet to slow business investment as companies looked to build up more AI-related infrastructure last quarter. This story is developing and will be updated.

articles.body:
Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday.

The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025.

Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August.

The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August.

Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic’s restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed’s 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September.

On Wednesday, though, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to hold rates at a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent.

After that decision, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the weeks leading up the FOMC’s next meeting in early December will “provide more clarity” on the “appropriate protocol” for the committee regarding monetary policy.

“What we’ve done in this monetary medicine, it’s starting to work some, but there’s no firm conclusions,” Warsh said, referencing the Fed’s rate hike in September. “If we had a firm conclusion about the conduct of monetary policy, we’d announce it to much fanfare today.”

articles.title: DoorDash is buying Instacart for $17 billion
articles.summary: DoorDash is buying rival Instacart in a deal worth roughly $17 billion, signaling that the delivery wars continue to heat up.
articles.body: DoorDash is buying rival Instacart in a deal worth roughly $17 billion, signaling that the delivery wars continue to heat up. The deal, announced Thursday, marks an end for Instacart as an independent company. Instacart went public in 2023 and benefited from a pandemic-era boom for the grocery delivery service, but it has struggled to maintain its momentum against larger competitors, like Uber, Amazon and Walmart. Combining Instacart and DoorDash two would create a larger company that better competes with those rivals. Amazon, for example continues to expand its same-day grocery service, which now totals 2,300 locations, while Walmart now offers 30 minute delivery in some places. Meanwhile, Uber has expanded its offerings, recently inking a deal with Costco. DoorDash said in a press release that the combined company “will offer grocers and retailers of every size DoorDash’s delivery network and Instacart’s grocery and fulfillment technology.” DoorDash has been expanding its suite of services beyond meal delivery, including adding restaurant reservations and delivery products beyond food, striking partnerships with Home Depot and Sephora. Now, it can increase its business with more grocery options, too. “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts,” Tony Xu, the cofounder and CEO of DoorDash said in a statement. He added that Instacart “has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery.” The deal is a mix of cash and stock, with DoorDash paying $65 per share, marking a roughly 25% premium from Instacart’s October 22 close when media reports said that it was mulling a sale. The companies are touting the benefits of the combination, including that people won’t have to buy two membership programs (DashPass and Instacart+), which could save its customers an “estimated $100 million per year on membership fees alone.” But there’s already opposition to the deal, with the American Economic Liberties Project (AELP), an anti-monopoly advocacy group, pushing regulators to block the deal because it would control nearly 60% of the third-party grocery delivery market. “Instacart and Doordash have spent the better part of a decade bullying main street businesses and denying fair pay and benefits to their combined 9 million workers,” said Lee Hepner, Senior Legal Counsel at the AELP, in a statement. “This merger represents the next frontier of data-driven abuse, exploiting massive asymmetries of power to squeeze worker compensation on the way in and drain consumer wallets on the way out.” The combination, which is expected to close in the coming months, is one of many in the delivery space. Grubhub’s US business was sold to Wonder for $650 million in 2025, and Uber bought European company Delivery Hero this summer for $14.8 billion. In 2020, Uber bought Postmates for $2.65 billion.

articles.title: Utah charges Kalshi and its founders, escalating a fight over who can regulate prediction markets
articles.summary: Utah on Wednesday filed criminal charges against prediction market operator Kalshi and two of its executives, months after a federal judge rejected Kalshi's effort to prevent Utah from enforcing its strict anti-gambling laws against the activity.
articles.body: Utah on Wednesday filed criminal charges against prediction market operator Kalshi and two of its executives, months after a federal judge rejected Kalshi's effort to prevent Utah from enforcing its strict anti-gambling laws against the activity. The felony charges could represent a new tactic in how states try to assert regulatory authority over the fast-expanding activity, a clash that appears headed to a showdown at the U.S. Supreme Court. The charges include 13 counts of violating the state's prohibition on gambling and another charge involving profiting off illegal activity. The state's charging documents name Kalshi and its co-founders, chief executive officer Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara. In a statement, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown said Kalshi has continued to operate in Utah, despite a federal court ruling that Utah's gambling laws apply to the company. “Gambling is illegal in Utah, whether you place the bet, run the game, or promote it. Calling it a ‘prediction market’ doesn’t change what it is, and being federally registered doesn’t put a company above the law," Brown said in a statement. The attorney general's office did not immediately say what sort of criminal penalties it would seek in the case, although the felony charges carry the possibility of jail time. In a statement, Kalshi called the charges a “crazy overreach” and said that “Utah is clearly playing politics.” “We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona,” it said. Utah has been on the front lines of a battle between states and the federal government over who regulates the markets. Litigation has spread across roughly 20 states, creating a fragmented legal landscape that analysts say will likely be settled by the U.S. Supreme Court. Kalshi has maintained that prediction markets fall exclusively under federal jurisdiction and are not governed by state gambling laws. Under President Donald Trump, the federal agency responsible for regulating financial markets, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, has agreed and even sued at least 10 states — including Utah this week — to try to stop states from regulating prediction markets. Arizona earlier this year became the first state to file criminal charges against Kalshi, accusing it of operating an illegal gambling business within its borders. A judge later put that case on hold. But one legal analyst, Daniel Wallach, said Arizona's authority to pursue the misdemeanor charges could soon be restored after the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco refused to let Kalshi restart trading on sports and elections events in Nevada while it fights the state’s effort to shut it down. Still, Utah's pursuit of felony charges represents a potential shift in strategy by states that have primarily pursued civil actions against prediction market operators, said Wallach, a lawyer who specializes in sports wagering and gaming law and teaches at the University of Miami School of Law. Wallach said he expects to see states bring more cases like Utah's and that Utah's criminal charges “could be a bellwether for how other states approach Kalshi and Polymarket" following Nevada's appellate court victory. Kalshi sued Utah in February, asking a federal judge to prevent the state from enforcing its gambling restrictions on the platform. The lawsuit came as Utah was on the verge of enacting legislation intended to undercut prediction markets from doing business in the state. A federal judge rejected the request, saying the federal law that Kalshi cited in its argument, the Commodity Exchange Act, doesn't prevent the state from enforcing its laws. The 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver last month declined to halt Utah's regulatory enforcement during Kalshi's appeal.
